圭の顔すら見る事が出来ない。: I couldn't even bring myself to look at Kei's face.
声から圭が興奮しているのは伝わる。: From his voice alone, I could tell he was excited.
無理もないだろう。昨日、アルバムで見てあれだけ興味を示していた少女が目の前にい: And no wonder. The girl he'd shown so much interest in when he saw her in the album yesterday was standing right in front of him.
「あ、あのですね。えっと、この街を離れている間、いろいろと様子が変わってました。: "U-um, so. While I've been away from this town, a lot has changed. I'm... so happy to be back."
「み、右も左も分からないふつつかものですが、よろしくお願いします」: "I-I'm still inexperienced and don't know my way around, but I hope you'll take good care of me."
自己紹介が終わった後、ドッと教室を笑いが包んだ。: When the self-introduction was over, a wave of laughter swept the classroom.
「御桜……嫁に来たんじゃないんだから、その言葉は正直どうかと思う」: "Misakura... you're not coming here as a bride, so honestly, I don't think that's quite the phrase to use."
ふと、窓から外を見る。: My eyes drifted to the window.
相変わらずの陽気にめまいすらする。: The sunshine was as clement as ever -- almost dizzying.
薄暗い教室から、薄紅の花弁が、地に触れては、離れるのを見つめる。: From the dim classroom, I watched pale crimson petals touch the ground, then lift away again.
不規則に舞い降りる花弁を横目で見ながら、俺は静かにまぶたを閉じる。: Watching the petals drift down in their irregular dance out of the corner of my eye, I quietly closed my eyelids.
始終、圭が大騒ぎしていたが、俺は始終無関心であった。: The whole time, Kei was a whirlwind of excitement, and the whole time, I remained indifferent.
切り離さなければいけない過去。: There are pasts one must sever.
忘れてやらなければならない絆。: There are bonds one must let oneself forget.
そういうものだってある……。: Such things exist in this world...
鈍そうでありながら、それなりに鋭い圭は、何かに感づいたのか、それとも飽きたのか: Kei may seem dull, but he's sharp enough in his own way. Whether he'd sensed something or simply lost interest, I don't know, but he stopped trying to talk to me much after that.
結局、ホームルームが終わるまで……。\n: In the end, until homeroom was over...
俺は、教室の最後尾から、稟の背中以外を見ることは無かった。: from the back row of the classroom, I saw nothing but Rin's back.
ホームルームが終わると、即座に放課後となる。: When homeroom ends, it's straight into after-school.
初日など学園生活にとっては顔見せみたいなものだろうか……。: The first day of school is really more of a "meet and greet" for student life, I suppose...
転校生である稟の周りにはクラスの女子が群がり始める。: The girls of the class were already flocking around Rin, the transfer student.
その周りにさらに男子が取り巻きはじめる。: And around them, the boys began to gather in turn.
「髪が超綺麗～。シャンプー、どこの使ってる？」: "Your hair's so gorgeous~. What shampoo do you use?"
「すごいなぁ。人間のバリケードに囲まれて、転校生の姿はすっかり見えなくなってしま: "Amazing. She's been walled up behind a human barricade -- the transfer student's vanished completely."
「俺があんなにはしゃいだから、へそ曲げてるのか？」: "You bent out of shape because I got so hyped up?"
「だったら挨拶ぐらいした方がいいんじゃないのか？」: "If not, wouldn't it be better to at least go say hi?"
「これから同じクラスなのだろ。だったら<r いや>否</r>が<r おう>応</: "We'll be in the same class from here on out. Which means, like it or not, I'll wind up saying hello sooner or later."
「どっちにしろ、あの人だかりをかき分けてかける言葉とかないだろ」: "Either way, there's nothing worth saying that I could shout through that crowd."
「もう少し落ち着いてからでいいだろ。あいつに話しかけるのは……」: "It'll be fine once things settle down. Talking to her, I mean..."
「ほら、いつまでも人だかりを見てても仕方がないだろ。いくぞ」: "Come on, no point standing here staring at a crowd forever. Let's go."
俺たちは、質問攻めに遭う稟を尻目に二人で教室を後にした。: Leaving Rin to fend off the interrogation, the two of us left the classroom together.
廊下には、新学期特有のざわめきが溢れている。: The corridor was filled with the particular buzz that only comes with a new school term.
早くも各部活の勧誘活動がはじまっており、各教室へのビラ配りや、窓から見える校庭: Club recruitment was already in full swing -- flyers being pushed at every classroom, and out the windows, the athletic clubs were putting on demonstrations in the schoolyard.
「美食を自負するならこの料理研究会へどうぞ！ 料理の腕を上げるだけでなく、夏には: "If you consider yourself a connoisseur, come join our Culinary Research Society! Not only will your cooking skills improve -- this summer we're doing a gourmet tour of Chinatown!"
「君も僕らと一緒に限界クロックアップに挑んでみないかっ！？ パソコンから火を吹い: "Won't you join us in pushing your machines to their absolute clock limits!? A true master makes his PC breathe fire -- come, one and all, to our Cyber Club!"
廊下の端々から、威勢のいい勧誘の声が上がる。どの部も、部員獲得のために趣向を凝: From every corner of the corridor came spirited pitches. Every club was doing everything it could think of to reel in new members.
そういえば美術部も、今日から数日に渡って勧誘を行うとか鳥谷が力説していた。: Come to think of it, Toritani had been going on about how the art club would be running its recruitment drive over the next several days, starting today.
「圭……俺は裏口から帰るつもりだ」: "Kei... I'm going home through the back gate."
「いや、正門はまずいだろう」: "No, the front gate's going to be trouble."
「この時期はまずいだろ。俺なんか毎年毎年関係ないのに大いに被害にあっている……」: "Not this time of year. Every single year I take heavy casualties even though it has nothing to do with me..."
「ふぅ……、ヤな感じね。美形と言われて、躊躇することなく振り返ったわね。ご自分で: "Hmph... What a nasty attitude. You turned around at 'handsome' without so much as hesitating. So you fancy yourself a looker, do you?"
「はぁ？ 御自負の問題じゃねぇだろ」: "Huh? It's not about fancying myself anything."
「その感じだと、何させられるか理解しているのでしょ？」: "Judging by the look on your face, you already understand what I'm about to make you do?"
「ボサっとつっ立ってないで、アンタもビラ配りに協力しなさい。はい、今日の分のノル: "Don't just stand there gawking, you're helping hand out flyers too. Here, your quota for today."
元気よくチラシの束が手にわたされる。: A stack of flyers was cheerfully thrust into my hands.
当然、俺の元気は瞬時に失われる。: Naturally, my cheer evaporated on the spot.
「何、エナジードレインでも喰らった様な顔してるのよ」: "What's with that face? Like something just Energy Drained you."
「何言ってるのよ。３６４日すべてダルそうに生きてるんだから、今日ぐらい元気を振り: "What are you saying? You live 364 days a year looking miserable, so today of all days you can wring out a little cheer! It's a new term!"
「さぁ、元気よく！ 気持ちよく！ がんっがん新入部員を勧誘しなさい！」: "Come on, cheerfully! Enthusiastically! Recruit those new members like there's no tomorrow!"
何故、３６４日ダルく生きてる人間が、新学期に突然元気にならなければならないのか: Why should someone who lives 364 days of the year in listless gloom suddenly get all cheerful just because it's a new term?
３６４日おとなしく、新学期だけ異様に元気ならば、それは狂っている人だろう。: If you were subdued for 364 days and then abruptly brimming with energy on the first day of term, you'd be a lunatic.
この日だけ狂った様に元気を出すなど不可能だ。: To fake enthusiasm like a madman for this one day alone is impossible.
「何、ぶつぶつ言ってるのよ！ さぁ元気を出してっ」: "What are you muttering about?! Come on, put your back into it!"
仕方なく……俺は彼女の期待に応えて元気を絞り出す。: Reluctantly... I mustered up cheer to meet her expectations.
３６４日いつもダルい（鳥谷基準で）俺は元気を振り絞る。: I -- who am listless 364 days a year (by Toritani's standard) -- summoned up my energy.
「よし！ せっかくだから俺は元気に断るぜ！」: "Alright! Since I'm at it, I'll refuse cheerfully!"
「そ、そんな元気よく殴るなよぅ。少し痛いわ……」: "D-don't punch me so cheerfully. That kind of hurts..."
「ご、ごめんなさい……。でも、そんな笑顔で言われたら脊髄反射で殴りもすると思うわ: "S-sorry... But if someone said that to you with a grin like that, you'd punch them on pure reflex. Even someone who isn't me..."
「たしかに、今のは純度１００％の元気な笑顔だったな。横にいた俺でも少しイラッとし: "It's true, that just now was a hundred-percent-pure cheerful smile. Even standing next to you, I got a little annoyed..."
「なぜ、元気な笑顔にむかつくんだ？ <r えーしぃー>公共広告奇行</r>に喧嘩: "Why does a cheerful smile make you mad? You picking a fight with the public service announcements or something?"
「いや、あのタイミングは普通にむかつくと思うけど……」: "No, I mean, the timing there would piss anyone off..."
「タイミングなどどうでもいい！ 俺は断る！ 元気よく断る！ 何度も言うが俺は美術: "Timing doesn't matter! I refuse! I cheerfully refuse! I'll say it again and again -- I am not a member of the art club."
「そういう事は部室を好き勝手使うのをやめてから言うことね。だいたいこの間大量のイ: "You can say that once you've stopped using the club room however you please. And by the way, you knocked over a whole pile of easels the other day and just left, didn't you!"
そういえば草薙健一郎が使っていたイーゼルを取りに行った時に崩してしまったのを放: Now that she mentioned it, when I'd gone in to fetch the easel Kusanagi Ken'ichirou had used, I'd sent them tumbling and left them where they fell.
「ほら、ほら、いいわけなんて聞かないからね、ほらこのチラシを持ちなさい！」: "Come on, come on, I'm not listening to your excuses. Here, take these flyers too!"
先ほど渡されたチラシの上に、さらなるチラシが乗せられる。: Another wad of flyers was piled on top of the ones I already had.
「そりゃ、ウチの部の命運がかかってるんだから、当然よ！」: "Well, of course -- the fate of our club rides on this!"
「どこで配るんだ？ こんな量……」: "Where am I supposed to hand out this many...?"
「中央広場で配ってくれるかしら？ あそこが新入生争奪戦の激戦区だから」: "Would you distribute them at the central plaza? That's the fiercest battleground for grabbing new students."
「あなたには、あなたしか出来ない特別ミッションを考えてるの。明日のためのね」: "I've got a special mission cooked up that only you can do. For tomorrow."
「俺しか出来ないミッションか？ それはすごいぞ」: "A mission only I can do? That's amazing!"
こいつは学習能力という機能がないのだろうか？: Does he not have a function called "learning ability"?
毎年繰り返される悲劇……というか喜劇……。: A tragedy repeated every year... no, a farce, more like.
こいつに下されるミッションなんぞ、毎年同じものなんだけどな。: The mission handed down to him is exactly the same, every single year.
「さすが、圭だなー。お前だけのミッションだー。俺にはもちろん鳥谷にも出来ない大事: "Wow, as expected of Kei. It's a mission for you alone. An important job that neither I nor even Toritani can do. Good luck out there."
「おお！ 直哉も応援してくれるか！ 俺がんばるぞ！」: "Ooh! Even Naoya's cheering me on! I'll do my best!"
二人は校舎に消えていく。: The two of them vanished into the school building.
ドナドナと……。: Off to market, off to market...
弓張学園の敷地の中には、何故か教会が存在している。: For some reason, within the grounds of Yumihari Academy, there stands a church.
そこがおしゃれだとかで、この学校を志望する学生さんが後を絶たない。: Apparently it's considered stylish, and there's no end to the students who apply to this school on account of it.
そんな教会の前には、ちょっとした広場が設けられており、そこは学生たちの憩いの場: Before that church is a small plaza which has become a hangout for the students.
アンフィテアトルムと名付けられた半円形劇場。: A semicircular theater called the Amphitheatrum.
演劇や演奏、声楽発表などに使われるものらしいが、\n: Supposedly it's used for plays, performances, and vocal recitals,
これが文化祭以外にその様な用途で使われている姿など見たことがない。: but I've never once seen it used for any such thing outside of the culture festival.
<r アンフィテアトルム>半円形劇場</r>はだいたいは学生のたむろする場とし: The semicircular theater is used mostly just as a place for students to loiter.
とりあえず、ここで午後のティータイム（だいたいペットボトルの紅茶）やら談話など: Apparently, whiling away an afternoon tea-time here (usually with bottled tea) or chatting about this and that qualifies as "Yumihari-style youthful chic."
全体的に中世ヨーロッパのゴシック様式をふんだんに取り入れた建築物である弓張学園: Yumihari Academy is a structure that generously incorporates the Gothic style of medieval Europe throughout -- and yet no one questions the incongruous presence of an Amphitheatrum, an architectural form from the Roman era.
奴らはおしゃれを満喫している。: They just bask in the "chic" of it all.
広場には、既に数人の生徒たちが、思い思いのスタイルで時間を潰していた。: In the plaza, several students were already killing time in whatever pose suited them.
人生について語り合う若者、アコギをゆっくりと爪弾き脱原発を訴える若者、電話帳を: Youths debating life, youths slowly strumming acoustic guitars while calling for the end of nuclear power, youths reading phone directories, youths conferring about their spring event's new releases.
それらを――有り余る若さを燃やす若者達を――囲むように、桜は萌える様に咲き誇る: Around them -- around these youths burning off their excess of youth -- the cherry blossoms bloomed in riotous vigor, as if in benediction over this purgatorial youth-hell...
どうも心が殺伐としているのか、碌な事を考えない。: My heart must have been in a bleak mood -- nothing decent was coming into my head.
しかし、こいつらはなんでこんな場所にたむろっているのだろうか……。: But really, why do these people hang around in a place like this...
人がいなければ、いくら鳥谷でもチラシなど配ろうとは思わないだろう。: If nobody were here, even Toritani wouldn't try to hand out flyers.
無駄に人がわらわら涌いているから鳥谷もチラシなど配ろうと考えるのだろう。: It's precisely because people are milling about pointlessly that Toritani gets it into her head to distribute them.
「とりあえず早急に終わらせて帰ろう……」: "For now, let's finish this up as fast as possible and go home..."
薄紅の花弁が、肩に触れては離れ。: Pale crimson petals brushed my shoulder and were gone again.
不規則に舞い降りる花弁を横目で見ながら、俺は静かに残りのチラシを配っていく。: Watching the irregular fall of the petals out of the corner of my eye, I quietly went on handing out the remaining flyers.
黙々とやっていると、知らぬ間にいらぬ事が頭を支配し始める。: Working in silence, before I knew it, thoughts I didn't want began to take over my mind.
無論、今の俺の心を支配していたのは、美術部のチラシ配りに専念することでも、鳥谷: What now held my heart was not, of course, my devotion to distributing the art club's flyers, nor Toritani's recruitment strategy.
考えたくもない事が、思い出したくない事が、知らぬ間に心を支配している。: Things I didn't want to think about, things I didn't want to remember, had crept in and taken hold before I noticed.
――突如、俺の前に現れた、遠い日の幼なじみの事。: -- The childhood friend from those distant days, who had suddenly reappeared before me.
なぜ、突然、あいつはこの街に戻ってきたんだろうか……。: Why had she come back to this town, so suddenly...
なぜ、俺は彼女から目線をそらしてしまったのだろうか……。: Why had I looked away from her...
「ったく……俺は軟弱な男だな」: "Good grief... what a spineless man I am."
桜の花弁を宙に舞わせる。: Cherry petals were sent whirling through the air.
一瞬、視界が、紅色の世界に支配される。: For a moment, my whole field of vision was overtaken by a world of crimson.
突然の風が、一枚のチラシを、手元からさらった。: A sudden gust snatched one of the flyers right out of my hand.
とっさに手を伸ばしたが、チラシは指先にかすりもせずに、軽やかに虚空に舞い上がる: I reached out reflexively, but the flyer slipped past my fingertips without so much as brushing them, dancing lightly up into the void.
風が弱まり、チラシはようやく高度を下げて、ゆっくりと地面へと降下を始める。俺は: As the wind died down, the flyer finally lost altitude and began its slow descent to the ground. Guessing where it would land, I set off slowly after it.
乾いた音を立てて、チラシは地面へと舞い降りる。: With a dry little sound, the flyer alighted on the ground.
俺は腰を曲げて、チラシを拾い上げようと。: I bent at the waist, meaning to pick the flyer up.
拾い上げようと、した――。: Meaning, that is, to pick it up--.
しかし、それより先に、チラシを拾い上げる手。: But before I could, another hand was already reaching for it.
チラシを拾い上げた人物は、俺の方に向き直り――。: The person who picked up the flyer turned to face me--.
その瞳を、真っ直ぐに、俺に向けた。: And fixed those eyes of theirs, straight, on me.
薄紅の世界から浮かび上がるように、その人物は一歩前に踏み出すと、手にしたチラシ: As if surfacing from a world of pale crimson, the figure took a step forward, and slowly held the flyer out to me.
世界を、刻を――染め上げていた。: Was dyeing the world, was dyeing the moment--in its color.
「もー、なおくんはそんなまた悲しいことを言う」: "Mou-- Nao-kun says such sad things again."
「そうだよ。それは悲しいことだよ」: "Yes. That's a sad thing to say."
「そうなんだ。でも俺が考えた言葉じゃないけど」: "I see. Though those aren't my own words."
「なおくん……、\nでもなおくんもそう思ってるんでしょ。\nそう思ってるから――: "Nao-kun... but you think so too, don't you? Because you think so--"
「だめだよっ。そんなことしたらみんないなくなっちゃうよ！」: "You can't! If you do that, everyone will be gone!"
「だったら、大切な人を作らなければいい」: "Then all I have to do is not make anyone precious to me."
「大切な人がいなければ、死ぬ必要がない……のかも」: "If there's no one precious to me, I won't need to die... probably."
「ば、ばかっ！ ばかばかばか！ なおくんのばかっ！！」: "S-stupid! Stupid stupid stupid! Nao-kun, you idiot!!"
「それじゃ……、それじゃみんながおんなじ時間に、おんなじ場所で生きてる意味がない: "If that's how it is... if that's how it is, then there's no meaning in everyone living in the same time and the same place!"
「もう知らないっ！ なおくんのばかばかばか！」: "I don't care anymore! Nao-kun, stupid stupid stupid!"
走り去る稟の姿。: Rin's figure as she ran off.
俺はただその背中をみていた。: I just watched her back as she went.
たいした考えがあった言葉では無かった。: They weren't words spoken with any deep thought.
ただ印象深く、幼き俺に響いた言葉。: Just words that struck deep, that lingered in me when I was young.
いや、分かるはずも無い。: No, there was no way I could have understood.
なるほど、喜び過ぎず悲しみ過ぎずか。: Ah yes--neither too joyful nor too sorrowful.
あの日を越えた、今なら分かる。: Now, having passed through that day, I understand.
春の日の狂想。: A rhapsody of a spring day.
ただ幼き稟の後ろ姿をみていた。: I simply watched Rin's small retreating figure.
目をつぶるとそんなものが浮かぶ。: Close my eyes and such things rise up before me.
テンポ正しく、握手をしませう。: In perfect tempo, let us shake hands.
古い雨戸を開け、早朝の空気を取り入れる。: Sliding open the old storm shutters, I let in the early morning air.
朝靄のかかった庭。: The garden veiled in morning mist.
冷たい空気が少し心地よい。: The cold air felt somehow pleasant.
寝不足でほてった身体に、春先の冷たい空気が心地よい……。: The chill of early spring air felt good against a body flushed from lack of sleep......
寝られなくなる様な理由では無かったはずなのになぁ。: There shouldn't have been any reason I'd lose sleep over it.
なんやかんや気にしているのか……。: Was it bothering me one way or another......?
ただ、その当たり前の言葉が、俺には痛かった。: Yet those ordinary words hurt me.
<r うら>恨</r>んでないんだなぁ。: She doesn't resent me at all, huh.
あいつらしいといえばあいつらしい……。: Very much like her, I suppose......
一回もあいつからの手紙に、俺は返事を書いてやらなかったのになぁ。: Even though I never once wrote back to a single one of her letters.
「にもかかわらず。笑顔で“ただいま”か」: "And still, she smiled and said 'I'm home.'"
これじゃ、完全に俺が悪者だな……。: This makes me the villain, plain and simple......
まぁ、悪者と言えば悪者だ。: Well, if you called me a villain, I'd be a villain.
俺は大嘘つきなんだからな。: Because I'm one hell of a liar.
「さすが、自称美の巨匠だな。美とやらを見る目がある」: "As expected of the self-proclaimed master of beauty. He has an eye for the stuff."
とは言っても、女に対する審美眼で、美の巨匠というのもなんだかな話ではあるが。: Though calling him a master of beauty for his aesthetic eye when it comes to women is... something else.
身長も、髪もだいぶ伸びてた。: Both her height and her hair had grown considerably.
そういえば……。: Now that I think of it......
あれから時間が経ったんだな……。: Time really has passed since then......
湿っぽいのは得意じゃない。: I'm not much for the sentimental.
そう言ったのは俺自身のはずだ。: Those were my own words, weren't they.

「主に愛液と唾液で自室が」: "My room, mostly with love-juice and saliva."
大海原をゆっくりと、確実に、進む船が、海を蹴立てゆく波の音は、まるで、この夜が: The sound of waves kicked up by a ship advancing slowly, surely across the vast open sea is so pleasant that one begins to think this night might go on forever -- and before one knows it, sleep itself is broken.
あまりに心地よいために目覚める夢。: A dream from which one wakes because it is too pleasant.
そういったものだってあるのだろう……。: Perhaps there are dreams like that too......
<r はら>祓</r>い清められた空気の中、: Within air that had been purified by ritual,
私はずっとそこに座っていた。: I had been sitting there all along.
正面の<r みす>御簾</r>。: The bamboo blind directly before me.
その向こうに横たわる人影――その名はたしか中村<r ときつな>時綱</r>と言: The human figure lying beyond it -- his name, if I recall, was Nakamura Tokitsuna.
彼の眠りが夢に達した時、詠唱が始まる。: When his sleep reaches the depth of dreaming, the incantation begins.

その鈴の名は「伯奇神楽鈴」。: That bell is called the "Hakuki Kagura Bell."
灘の儀に方相が伯奇の力をより良く引き出す時に使う。: It is used in the Nada rite, when the Hososhi draws forth the powers of Hakuki to their fullest.
さらに、その鈴は私と方相氏を結びつける神具でもあった。: Moreover, that bell was a sacred implement binding me and the Hososhi together.
方相氏の声に、かすかにゆれた意識が<r しず>鎮</r>まる。: My consciousness, which had faintly wavered, is stilled by the voice of the Hososhi.
御簾の向こうに横たわる当主時綱を、静かに見つめる。: I gaze quietly at the lord Tokitsuna, lying beyond the blind.
ただ永遠に続く夢を見る。: To dream a dream that goes on eternally.
朝の訪れを待つほどに――: Even to the coming of the morning --
器に夢が張られる。: A dream is drawn into the vessel.
その奥底は、手に収まるほどの器であるにもかかわらず、まるでのぞき込む事が出来な: Its depths, though the vessel is small enough to hold in one's hand, feel so deep that one cannot peer to the bottom.
正面の御簾。\n: The bamboo blind directly before me.
その奥にいる男の夢。: The dream of the man who lies beyond it.
私は器に手をつける。: I place my hand upon the vessel.
そして、そっと口をつけ。: And then, gently, I bring it to my lips.
深く、深く、どこまでも続く透明な夢。: Deep, deep, a transparent dream that goes on without end.
私はその夢の中に沈んでいく。: I sink down into that dream.
底に、底に沈んでいく。: Down to the bottom, sinking to the bottom.
だけれども、それはここよりさらに水底。: But it is even further below than where I am.
仄かに水面が揺らめく。: Faintly, the surface of the water ripples.
憎悪という揺らめきが私に囁く。: The rippling called hatred whispers to me.
それは、たぶん「憎い」という囁き。: It is, perhaps, a whisper of "I hate."
仄暗い夢の水底に沈んでいく。: I sink deeper into the dim water-bottom of the dream.
「<r いくさば>戦場</r>では父を立てたがために、<r おの>己</r>が: "On the battlefield, because I upheld my father, I could win no martial glory of my own."

「その恩を忘れ、儂を恨むとは」: "And forgetting that debt, they hold a grudge against me!"

何故か優美は探る様に私に尋ねる。: For some reason, Yumi asked me as if probing.
隠すことでも無いので、私は素直に答えた。: Since there was nothing to hide, I answered honestly.

私は昨日、そして今日続けて見た夢を優美に説明した。: I explained to Yumi the dream I had had yesterday, and again today.
細部に至るまでの説明は難しかったが、それでも説明出来る範囲では説明をした。: Explaining every detail was difficult, but I explained what I could.

「年端もいかない女の子が、京の都から落ち延びてきたのだから、不安とか、驚きとか、: "You'd think a young girl who had fled from the capital in Kyoto would feel anxiety, or surprise, or fear -- the sorts of things one usually would -- but she doesn't seem to feel any of that."
「誰に会っても、誰と話しても、何があっても、彼女は何も感じない」: "No matter whom she meets, no matter whom she speaks with, no matter what happens, she feels nothing."
「むしろ感情の起伏が無いというよりは、そう、心が無いみたいな感じ」: "Rather than saying she has no emotional range, it's more like -- yes, like she has no heart at all."

夢を飲むという事は、まるで他人の心が、そのものを受け入れる様なものなの……」: To drink a dream is like taking another person's heart, that very thing, into oneself......"

「いいえ、何でも無いわ。とりあえず全体的に分かった」: "No, it's nothing. Anyway, I get the overall picture."

長らく弓張に住んでいるが、こんなまじまじと伯奇神社を見るのははじめてだ。: I'd lived in Yumihari for ages, but this was the first time I'd looked at Hakuki Shrine so closely.

人が寝ているところを、何を耳元で物騒な事をつぶやいてる！」: Why are you muttering such alarming things by someone's ear while they're sleeping!"

「あれな。一種病気なんじゃねぇか？ って思うんだ」: "It's like -- I think it might be a kind of sickness."
「稟はな。道路を鏡にして、そして世界を逆転させた」: "Rin, she turned the road into a mirror and inverted the world."
「道路を鏡に？ 世界を逆転？ なんだそりゃ？」: "Turned the road into a mirror? Inverted the world? What's that supposed to mean?"
「道路いっぱいに、その道路から見える風景画を描いてたんだ。そのデッサンがあまりに: "She had drawn a landscape of the scene visible from that road, filling the whole road with it. The draftsmanship was so precise, that alone shook me."
「あんたが言うのだったら相当なものだったんだろうな」: "If you say so, it must have been really something."
「相当なんてもんじゃねぇよ。ほとんど写真だ。デッサンなんてレベルじゃない」: "It was more than 'something.' It was practically a photograph. It wasn't at the level of mere draftsmanship."
「あまりの出来だったんで、俺が立ち止まって見ていたら、稟は言った」: "It was so remarkable that when I stopped to look, Rin said,"
「世界は、その立ち位置からじゃ変わらないよ。ってな。\n場所を指さした」:
"'The world won't change from where you're standing.'
And she pointed to a spot."
「俺も一瞬意味が分からなかった。\nだから稟が指さした場所に立ったんだよ」:
"I didn't get what she meant at first.
So I stood at the spot Rin pointed to."
「そしたら、それまで、ただ精密なだけに見えたデッサンが、突如本来の姿を見せた」: "And then, the drawing that until then had only looked precise suddenly revealed its true form."
「その位置に立たなければ、その絵は大きな歪みを持った絵でしかなかった。\nだが、:
"If you didn't stand in that exact spot, the picture was just a heavily distorted image.
But the instant I stood where Rin pointed--"
「まるで風景がそのまま道路に映り込んだみたいに見えた」: "It looked as if the scenery itself had been reflected onto the road."
「道路に風景がそのまま映り込んだ様に？」: "Onto the road, as if reflected there?"
「ああ、蝋石だからさ、なんつーか白色が蜃気楼みたいに見えて、本当に道路にその風景: "Yeah, because it was wax stone -- the white looked something like a mirage, and it really did seem as if the scenery was projected onto the road."
「そりゃ、スーパーリアリズムみたいに写真を元にするやり方なら、手順さえ踏めば、あ: "Well, if you use a method like Superrealism, based on photographs, anyone can do it to some degree so long as they follow the procedure and have some patience."
「だが、稟が描いたものは、定位置でしか正しく見えない絵だ。他の場所から見たら歪ん: "But what Rin drew was a picture that could only be seen correctly from a fixed position. From anywhere else, it would look distorted."
「しかも、一発描きで、道路という巨大なキャンバスに、本物にしか見えない絵を仕上げ: "And on top of that, in a single pass, she had finished a picture that looked utterly real on the enormous canvas that is a road."
「たしかに、それだけ聞くと並大抵ではないが……」: "Certainly, just hearing that, it's no ordinary feat......"
「だが、一番恐ろしいのは、そのデッサン力ではない」: "But the most terrifying thing wasn't her draftsmanship."
「デッサン力はその手段でしかない。あの娘は蝋石で蜃気楼の様にあえて描く事によって: "Her draftsmanship was merely the means. That girl, by deliberately drawing with wax stone in a way like a mirage, turned the road into a mirror reflecting the world."
「そして鏡の世界。そう道路に映りこんだ世界こそが、まるで本物であるかの様な錯覚に: "And the world in the mirror -- the world reflected onto the road -- was what made you fall into the illusion that it was the real one."
「まさに、世界の見え方が一瞬変わったんだよ。\nそれこそ、あいつが描いたぼんやり:
"It's truly as if the way the world looked changed in an instant.
As if the vague, whitish world she had drawn was the real one, and this crisp world on our side was the fake."
「そんな馬鹿な事があるか？ 百歩ゆずって鏡に映る蜃気楼みたいな世界を再現出来たと: "Can something that absurd even happen? Even granting for the sake of argument that she reproduced a mirage-like world in the mirror, could you really feel more reality from that side?"
「だから、それが出来るのが御桜稟なんだよ」: "That's why -- that's exactly what Misakura Rin can do."
「道路、さらにいえば蝋石の様な儚いもので描かれた世界。そちらこそが本物であるかの: "A world drawn with something as ephemeral as wax stone, on a road no less. The illusion that that side is the real one."
「なんだ、それ？ それはさすがに親父の思い過ごしじゃないか？ 単に絵のデッサンが: "What is that? Isn't that just your imagination, old man? Her draftsmanship was just so tremendous that for a moment it looked that way......"
「おれも最初はそう思った。だが違う」: "I thought the same at first. But I was wrong."
「よくよく、見てみると、すべてが計算されている。ある立ち位置で、一瞬で世界の見え: "When you looked closely, everything was calculated. Down to a single line, it had been meticulously calculated so that, from a certain vantage point, the way the world looked would be transformed in an instant."
「それに彼女はあの時に俺に聞いた」: "And she asked me a question, back then."
「おじさんの中に神様はいるの？」: "Is there a god inside you, mister?"
「そのままの意味だろうな。俺の中に美の神様がいるのかって事だろ？」: "Exactly what it says, I'd guess. She was asking whether the god of beauty dwelt within me."
「当然、稟は言ったよ。“私の中に神様がいる”ってな。\nだから、いくらでも美しい:
"Naturally, Rin said, 'There's a god inside me.'
That's why she could produce beautiful things without end......"
「神は世界を七日間で作ったんだ。\nだったら神が宿った少女には何が作れる？」:
"God made the world in seven days.
Then what could a girl in whom a god dwells make?"
「さぁな、それが本当ならば、なんでも出来るんじゃないか？」: "Who knows. If it's really true, then anything, I suppose."
「ああ実際、彼女には通常では考えられないイマジネーションがある。\nそしてそれを:
"Well, in fact, she has an imagination beyond anything ordinary.
And she has a terrifying power to give it concrete form."
「具現化能力……なんだその言い方」: "Power to give it form... what a way to put it."
「あれはもう絵とかの創作のレベルじゃない。具現化だよ。\nあの娘の脳みそには、常:
"It's no longer at the level of painting or creation. It's manifestation.
Inside that girl's head are every kind of image an ordinary person could never conceive, and she just builds them up in the real world."
「だから、あれは絵画ではなく、イメージの具現化だ。\n彼女が自分の中に神を見たと:
"So it's not painting -- it's the manifestation of images.
Even if she claims to see a god within herself, it wouldn't exactly be wrong."
「聞いてる限りにおいてはな。\nだが、にわかに信じがたい」:
"So long as I'm only listening, sure.
But it's hard to believe on the spot."
「そりゃ、そうだ。実物を見てみないかぎり、あの娘の恐ろしいまでの力は分からない」: "Of course. Unless you see her work in person, you can't grasp the terrifying scale of that girl's power."
「創作ではなく具現化。才能では無く、特殊能力か。\nまるで超能力だな」:
"Not creation but manifestation. Not talent but a special ability.
It's practically a superpower."
「まるでそんな感じだ」: "That's just about the feel of it."
「少なくとも俺が知っている稟は、絵など描いてなかったが？」: "At least the Rin I knew didn't paint anything."
「なんでだろうなぁ。その辺りは俺も良く分からん。\n才能の塊の稟に、お前がどう映:
"I wonder why. Even I don't really know about that.
How you looked to Rin, a girl who was a lump of talent... I couldn't tell you."
「なんか知らんが、俺よりも評価が高かったし……」: "For some reason, she rated you higher than me..."
「いいや、何でも無い。お前が知る必要はない」: "No, never mind. You don't need to know."
「どちらにしても、俺としてはあまりお前と絵で接触してほしくないとは思ったさ」: "In any case, I did think I'd rather you two not come into contact through painting."
「なんだ？ 俺がヤツの絵を見て絶望するとでも思ったのか？」: "What? Did you think I'd fall into despair seeing that girl's paintings?"
「いや、タイミング……そういうものかもしれない」: "No, timing... maybe it was that kind of thing."
「お前は英才教育で育てたかったが、アメリカを飛び出して日本に帰ってきた」: "I wanted to raise you with an elite education, but you ran off from America and came back to Japan."
「マザコン？ まぁ、それもあるだろうけど、単に母親が心配だったんだろ？」: "Mama's boy? Well, there's that too, but you were just worried about your mother, weren't you?"
「幼いお前だって、夏目家と中村家の騒動は知っていた」: "Even young as you were, you knew about the trouble between the Natsume and Nakamura households."
「水菜に関して一応の決着がついていたとはいえ、母親一人にするのは耐えられなかった: "Even if things had been more or less settled where Mizuna was concerned, you couldn't stand leaving your mother alone, could you?"
「夏目の婆さんが死んでなければ、俺も同じ事を言って、何の気兼ねなくニューヨークで: "If the Natsume grandmother hadn't died, I'd have said the same thing myself, and I could have worked in New York with no reservations at all."
「お前がニューヨークから日本に帰国したのは、夏目琴子婆さんが死んでからだ」: "It was after Grandma Natsume Kotoko died that you came back to Japan from New York."
「事実、俺自身、水菜を一人にするのは気が引けたもんだ。夏目の婆さんが死んでからは: "The truth is, I felt uneasy about leaving Mizuna alone myself. After Grandma Natsume died, I heard people who looked like Nakamura men started skulking around the estate."
「でも、母さんはあんたにニューヨークで仕事をしてくれと言っていた」: "But Mom told you to keep working in New York."
「ああ、そうだ。しゃーないよな。水菜の身柄は借金という形で身の安全を保証されてい: "Yeah, she did. It couldn't be helped. Mizuna's safety is only guaranteed in the form of a debt. If I don't earn, nothing works out."
「どっちにしろ英才教育はほどこせなかった」: "Either way, I couldn't give you an elite education."
「なんだ？ それに対する当てつけの弟子か？」: "What -- so the disciple was some kind of spite over that?"
「いやいや、稟に教えた時間なんて、お前に教えた時間の数十分の一程度だよ」: "No, no. The time I spent teaching Rin was maybe a few dozenths of what I spent teaching you."
「だが、あんたが唯一認める弟子なんだろ？」: "But she's the only disciple you'll acknowledge, isn't she?"
「俺は稟に<r えが>描</r>くという事を教えた」: "What I taught Rin was what it means to paint."
「<r えが>描</r>くという事？ デッサンを教えたという意味か？」: "What it means to paint? You mean you taught her drawing?"
「違う。俺は彼女に芸術という事を教えた。\nあれに、基礎デッサンやら教えても仕方:
"No. What I taught her was art.
There was no point teaching that girl basic draftsmanship -- she was better at it than me."
「あの娘には、たしかに天才的なイマジネーションがあったが、芸術というのはそれだけ: "That girl certainly had a genius imagination, but art isn't only that."
「いや、逆に言えば、俺は芸術という楔によって、彼女のイマジネーションに縛りをかけ: "Or rather, put the other way, I used the wedge of art to bind her imagination."
「あの娘が描く絵は、人間が描く様なものではない」: "The paintings that girl makes aren't the sort of thing a human paints."
「たぶん、彼女が無自覚にイマジネーションをふくらましていき、それを具現化し続けた: "Probably, if she kept swelling her imagination unconsciously and manifesting it, she wouldn't be able to stay normal."
「普通ではいられないって、どうなるんだよ」: "Wouldn't stay normal -- what does that mean, exactly?"
「さぁな。それは分からない。ただ、あれは人の身体で許されるものではない」: "Who knows. I can't say. All I know is that thing isn't something a human body is permitted to hold."
「美は語り得ぬものだ。そう神秘主義者は言う」: "Beauty is the unspeakable. So say the mystics."
「だから、彼女には、芸術という、一種人間的なものを教えたんだよ」: "That's why I taught her a thing called art -- something of a kind that's human."
「芸術という人間的なものか。まぁ、人間ぐらいしかやらないからな」: "Something human, called art. Well, humans are about the only ones who do it."
「俺の言葉だ。とは言っても、元ネタはマシュー・アーノルドだが」: "Mine. Though the original goes back to Matthew Arnold."
「誰でもいいだろ。教えたところで、お前の教養なんてたかだか知れてるのだから」: "Never mind who. There's no point telling you -- your general culture is only so deep."
「それよりも、芸術において批評とは何だと思う？ 直哉」: "More importantly, Naoya, what do you think criticism means in art?"
「批評家とか評論家とかがするやつだろ？」: "It's what critics and reviewers do, isn't it?"
「はぁ、そういう事言うヤツは三流。全然ダメ」: "Ha. Someone who says that is third-rate. No good at all."
「閉じた世界は芸術ではない。\nさらに言えば、閉じた世界は完璧ではいけない」:
"A closed world is not art.
And going further, a closed world must not be perfect."
「閉じた世界？ 完璧ではいけない？」: "A closed world? Must not be perfect?"
「ああ、そうだ。無音の桜の森で、音が鳴るという事はそういう事さ」: "That's right. That's what it means for a sound to ring out in a soundless forest of cherry blossoms."
「それってあんたの詞だよな？ 『横たわる櫻』に添えられた詞」: "Those are your words, aren't they? The verse that accompanies 'The Reclining Sakura.'"
「あの詞は難解すぎるし、さらにいえば今言う意味が全然分からない。\nあんたは、俺:
"That verse is too obscure, and even more, I don't understand at all what you're saying now.
Do you have any intention of explaining to me?"
「ああ、あるさ。これから簡単な解説でもするか？」: "Yeah, I do. Want me to give a simple commentary, then?"
「作品は死骸だ。\nただし腐らない死骸。綺麗な標本みたいなもんだな」:
"A work is a corpse.
But a corpse that doesn't rot. Something like a clean specimen."
「死骸は死骸。どんだけ完成度が高かろうが、死骸だ。\nだから世界が閉じていたら、:
"A corpse is a corpse. No matter how high its degree of completion, it's a corpse.
So if the world is closed, it remains a corpse forever."
「ややすると天才というのは閉じた世界で生きてしまうものさ。\nだって、その世界は:
"Geniuses, for all their gifts, tend to live inside a closed world.
After all, that world is perfect."
「御桜稟という少女はまさに天才だ。\n彼女の作品が閉じているという意味においても:
"The girl called Misakura Rin is precisely a genius.
In the sense, too, that her works are closed."
「そういった意味では芸術とは、天才的では無く、人間的だとも言える」: "In that sense, one could say art is not genius-like but human."
「芸術は閉じた世界ではないのだからな」: "Because art is not a closed world."
「御桜稟がそれほどの天才か……」: "So Misakura Rin is that much of a genius......"
「偉人が残した芸術論も聞かせてやったよ。アリストテレスとかさ」: "I also had her listen to the theories of art left behind by the great figures. Aristotle and the like."
「アリストテレスといえば有名なアレか？」: "Speaking of Aristotle -- you mean that famous line?"
「だが、稟には馴染まなかった様だな。まったく逆の思想がしっくり来た様だった。『芸: "But it didn't seem to suit Rin. The exact opposite thought seemed to sit better with her. She was fond of things like 'The Critic as Artist' and 'The Decay of Lying.'"
「なんだそりゃ？ 俺は知らないぞ。そんな本」: "What's that? I don't know. Books like that."
「お前には必要ない本だよ。\n世界すべてのものが、芸術の模倣品でしかないなんて思:
"They're not books you need.
The idea that everything in the world is nothing but an imitation of art -- it's incompatible with your artistic sensibility."
「唯美主義って言うんだけどな。まぁ、天才さんの稟には肌にあったのだろうよ」: "It's called aestheticism. Well, it probably suited a genius like Rin."
「だが、唯美主義も、他人の眼が介在する事を重要視しているから、閉じた天才の世界に: "But aestheticism, too, places importance on the intervention of another's eye -- so it was convenient for teaching Rin, who lived inside the closed world of a genius."
「葛と稟は、俺が引き合わせた」: "I was the one who introduced Kuzu and Rin."
「あの二人だったら、上手くいくと思ったんだろうな……」: "I thought those two would work out well together..."
「稟には、まず観客が必要だと思った。\nそれも、そう簡単に感動しない様な観客だ」:
"I thought that what Rin needed first of all was an audience.
And not just any audience -- one that wouldn't be easily moved."
「何故、感動したらダメなんだ？」: "Why is it bad to be moved?"
「稟にとって、他人の目なんて、なんの役にも立たない」: "For Rin, other people's eyes are of no use whatsoever."
「彼女は先天的に知っていたのだろう。あらゆる人間が自分よりも劣った美意識を持ち、: "She probably knew it innately. That every human being has a lesser sense of beauty than her own, a lesser imagination. Naturally, at the ultimate reaches of beauty she attains, an audience holds no value at all."
「俺ですら、あの娘の絵に、一瞬にして虜にさせられたんだ。\n彼女の絵は感動させて:
"Even I was captivated in an instant by that girl's paintings.
Her paintings move you -- that's a given. Other people's eyes are no measure at all."
「だってさぁ。あの娘って、二歳の時だか描いた絵で親御さんが驚いて、それ以来、親御: "Look, that girl -- when she was two years old, she supposedly drew a picture that startled her parents so badly that ever since, she never drew in front of them again."
「何故だ？ あそこの父親はたしか画家で画商だろ？\n娘がそんな天才なら喜ぶんじゃ:
"Why? Her father's a painter and a dealer, isn't he?
Wouldn't he be delighted if his daughter was that much of a genius?"
「だからさ。無意識で知ってたんだろ。親が自分よりも劣っている事を。\nそして、そ:
"That's just it. She knew, unconsciously. That her parents were lesser than her.
And she didn't want to admit it either."
「だから、親の前では絵を描かなかった」: "That's why she never drew in front of her parents."
「なるほど、それを聞くと、あんたが稟に感じていたものも少し分かるな……」: "I see. Hearing that, I understand a little of what you felt about Rin......"
「だろ？ 絵に関して、というよりも美に関して、生まれ持って呪われている様な娘だっ: "Right? She was a girl who was, when it came to painting -- or rather, when it came to beauty -- cursed from birth."
「それで、何故そんな稟と葛を会わせたんだ？」: "Then why did you introduce a girl like that to Kuzu?"
「あの当時。葛には感情という感情が無かった」: "Back then. Kuzu had no such thing as emotions."
「ああ、完全に伯奇として覚醒していたわけじゃないから、中村家には知られていなかっ: "Yeah. Since she hadn't fully awakened as Hakuki, the Nakamura family didn't know, but that was probably a state peculiar to a girl with Hakuki's disposition."
「俺は、そんな葛に、普通の女の子として、普通に生きられる様に、感情を与えたかった: "I wanted to give a girl like Kuzu emotions -- so that she could live as an ordinary girl, ordinarily."
「残念ながら、藍はもとより、画家である俺ですら葛に感情を与える事が出来なかった」: "Unfortunately, not Ai, and not even I, a painter, could give Kuzu emotions."
「だが、稟ならば、あるいはと思った。\n稟だったら、心を無から生み出す事すら可能:
"But I thought that Rin might.
With Rin, it even seemed possible to bring a heart into being out of nothing......"
「あんたらしからぬほどのべた褒めだな……」: "That's more sheer praise than sounds like you......"
「いいや、もう絵が描けないんだ。絵で嫉妬のしようがない」: "No. I can't paint anymore. There's no way for me to be jealous through painting."
「心を持たない少女に、心を宿す」: "To place a heart in a girl who has none."
「それは、天才稟を持ってしても容易なことでは無かった」: "Even for the genius Rin, it wasn't an easy thing."
「自分の絵を見ても、無反応な葛」: "A Kuzu who showed no reaction even to her paintings."
「そんな相手と、はじめて稟は出会った」: "For the first time, Rin had met such a person."
「だから稟は心を宿さない少女の前で、絵を描き続けた」: "So Rin went on painting in front of the girl who had no heart."
「この世のあるものすべて、\nそしてこの世にないもののすべて」:
"Everything in this world,
and everything that isn't in this world."
「この世のすべては元より、この世にないすべてなんか描けないだろ……」: "Everything in this world, let alone everything not in this world -- you can't paint that......"
「いいや、稟の絵には、他人にそう思わせるだけの力があった」: "No, Rin's paintings had the power to make others believe it."
「いってみれば美の化け物。美に呪われた少女」: "You could call her a monster of beauty. A girl cursed by beauty."
「そんな少女だから、葛に心を宿す事が出来た」: "Because she was such a girl, she was able to place a heart in Kuzu."
「葛を、伯奇から人間に変えたのは御桜稟だ」: "The one who changed Kuzu from Hakuki into a human was Misakura Rin."
「そして、稟に観客というものを与えたのは葛だ」: "And the one who gave Rin an audience was Kuzu."
「稟は、その時に、他人に作品を見せる喜びを知った」: "That was when Rin came to know the joy of showing her work to others."
「あれから、少しだけ、彼女の絵が閉じた世界では無くなった。\nとは言っても、やは:
"From then on, just a little, her paintings ceased to be a closed world.
Though even so, she kept painting things that seemed cursed by beauty."
「稟がそんなヤツだとは到底思えないが」: "I can't imagine Rin as that kind of person."
「稟は絵を描いてる時以外は、まるで穏和な少女だったからな。\n少し不器用なぐらい:
"When she wasn't painting, Rin was really a gentle girl.
Just a little awkward."
「根は優しいんだよ。あの娘は、ただ呪われていたとしか言いようが無いな」: "She's kind at the core. That girl -- there's no way to put it except that she was cursed."

I can't be certain, but at the pace he's going...

The man, now right behind the child, lifts a foot ever so slightly.
Just as I thought.

The man whirled around, startled.
I smiled amiably at him.

Thank goodness.
If she hadn't remembered, I'd have been blatantly suspicious.

She bowed her head with a little dip.

Toritani stopped in front of the painting displayed in city hall.

Onto the opened book, I let a great heap of candies scatter down.

Nei stared at me intently.

Opening the pouch, she carefully put the candies away.

多忙な校長をつかまえることができた頃には、夜になっていた。: By the time we managed to pin down the ever-busy headmaster, it was already evening.
事情を黙って最後まで聞いた校長が、俺と鳥谷を交互に見る。: Having listened to the whole account in silence, the headmaster looks from me to Toritani and back.

At the very least, that woman Reika hasn't the slightest doubt of it.

いやもうワガママにうんざりといったレベルじゃない。\nそれは、鳥谷もわかってい:
No, it's far past the level of "worn out by willfulness."
Toritani knows that too, and is deliberately choosing mild words.
あの弁護士は、麗華の無茶な要求に疲弊しきっている。\nそれに気づけない校長では:
That lawyer is utterly exhausted by Reika's unreasonable demands.
The headmaster isn't one to miss that.

「あのまま家に帰っても良かったのに、疲れたでしょ」: "You could've just gone straight home, you know. You must be tired."
キマイラにわざわざ一緒についてきた俺に、\n鳥谷が呆れたような視線を向ける。け:
Toritani, whom I'd insisted on accompanying all the way back to Chimera,
turns an exasperated look on me. But her voice carries a note of concern.

「そんなのわかってるわよ。……いいわ、聞かせて」: "I know that. ...All right, let's hear it."
俺の案を聞いて、鳥谷が真面目な表情で腕を組む。\n真剣に吟味しているのが、その:
Toritani listens to my proposal and folds her arms with a serious expression.

Making our way through the storeroom, we came to a door at the back.
Toritani drew out a key.

立体物と言ったのは、とても美術工芸品とは言えないようなジャンク品も、数多く並ん: I said three-dimensional objects, but a great many pieces on display were junk items you could hardly call arts or crafts.

Though I called them junk, they weren't utter trash --

なんとなく安心する。\nここは、人が住むような場所ではないような気がした。:

A moist, milky-white waxen texture,
and a soft form that put one in mind of drooping candy-work.

The openwork silhouettes of flowers and women

Toritani laid a hand on a red-lacquered wicker chest set on the next shelf.

The Nihonga was the Magpie painting the lawyer had shown us at Chimera the other day.

She repeated the same answer as when I'd asked before. But in her voice
there was a certain distinctive familiarity he did not try to hide.
「今となっては、ただ、それだけの関係だよ」: "By now, that's all our relationship amounts to."
夜に慣れた目を店内で瞬かせる。: My eyes, adjusted to the night, blinked as they took in the shop.
キマイラの店内は、普段よりもきらきらと眩しく感じられた。\n部屋中に飾られたお:
The interior of the Chimera felt more dazzlingly bright than usual.
Surely it was because of the handmade ornaments strung around the room.
「天の川と鵲の橋だ」: "The Milky Way and the bridge of magpies."
校長のつぶやきにあわせて見あげると、\n折り紙で作られた天の川が目に入ってきた:
Looking up at the headmaster's murmur,
I saw the Milky Way, made of folded paper.
「カササギの橋って、七夕の伝説でしたっけ」: "The bridge of magpies -- that was the Tanabata legend, wasn't it?"
「そうだよ。１年に一度、七夕の夜、\n織り姫と彦星を会わせるために、カササギたち:
"That's right. Once a year, on the night of Tanabata,
the magpies spread their wings to make a bridge, so Orihime and Hikoboshi may meet."
カササギの橋か。\n以前、それと似た話を鳥谷としたことを思い出す。:
The bridge of magpies, huh.
I remembered having spoken with Toritani about something similar before.
「君とよく似てるじゃないか」: "It resembles you rather well, doesn't it?"
「若い君が、何かの、誰かの、橋渡しになることを好むのは、\nあまり感心しないけど:
"That someone young like you takes pleasure in becoming a bridge
for something, or someone -- I can't say I entirely approve."
「まあ……好きでやってることなので」: "Well... it's something I do because I like it."
白い折り紙で作られた天の川に、カササギの橋、\nキラキラと光る金と銀の星々、舞:
The Milky Way of white folded paper, the bridge of magpies,
the glittering gold and silver stars, flowers as if dancing, paper moons...
じっと見あげる寧に気づいた。: I noticed Nei gazing up at them.
近づいて声をかける。\n寧は、吊された金色のペーパームーンを見つめていた。:
I walked over and spoke to her.
Nei was staring at a golden paper moon that hung above her.
あれを飾ったバイトの子に許可をもらおうと店内を見渡しているところに、\n校長が:
As I was looking around the shop for the part-timer who'd hung it up
to ask permission, the headmaster came over.
すぐに校長が、霧乃さんを連れて戻って来た。: The headmaster soon came back with Kirino-san.
バイトの子が向こうから、大きく腕で丸の形を作っている。\nＯＫということだろう:
From across the room the part-timer was making a big circle with her arms.
Meaning it was OK.
バイトの子が、丈夫な脚立を運んで来る。: The part-timer brought over a sturdy stepladder.
霧乃さんはおっかなびっくりその上に乗ると、\n紙の月をそっと取り外して、寧に渡:
Kirino-san climbed onto it timidly,
gently removed the paper moon, and handed it to Nei.
受け取った寧は、大切そうにそっと紙の月に触れて微笑んだ。: Nei took it, touched the paper moon softly as if it were precious, and smiled.
恩田親子を見つめる校長の目は優しかった。: The headmaster's eyes, watching the Onda mother and daughter, were gentle.
「気が利いてますね、鳥谷校長」: "That was thoughtful of you, Headmaster Toritani."
「ああ。他人だからよく見えるし、うまく働きかけられる」: "Yes. Precisely because we're strangers, I can see clearly and act well."
他人ならば、ということか。: Because they're strangers -- was that it?
――母親としては失格だからね。\nそう言った校長を、思い出す。:
-- Because as a mother, she's a failure.
Those words the headmaster had spoken came back to me.
少し離れたところで鳥谷が、\n紙の月で遊ぶ恩田親子を、静かに見守る校長を見てい:
A little way off, Toritani was watching --
watching the headmaster who quietly watched the Onda mother and daughter playing with the paper moon.
校長に向けられた鳥谷の視線は、何のわだかまりもなく、\nただ穏やかだった。:
The gaze Toritani directed at the headmaster held no lingering grievance;
it was simply calm.
けれど二人の距離は、ずっとそのままで、\nこの時間が終わる最後まで、そして終わ:
But the distance between the two of them stayed exactly as it was,
right until this time came to an end -- and even after it ended,
they never once drew any closer.
最後の机を元に戻して、ぐるりとキマイラを見渡す。: I put the last table back where it belonged and glanced around the Chimera.
パーティーは和やかなままに解散となり、片づけも終わった。: The party had broken up peacefully, and the cleanup was finished.
バイトの子たちもみんな帰った。: The part-timers had all gone home too.
「あ、それ、悪いけど上に持っていってくれる？」: "Ah -- sorry, could you take that upstairs?"
二人で、パーティーに使ったこまごまとした小物などを、\n鳥谷の部屋に運んでいく:
The two of us carried the various odds and ends we'd used for the party
up to Toritani's room.
「そういえば、鳥谷は、校長と話したのか？」: "Come to think of it -- did you speak with the headmaster?"
「ありがと。でも、私達はこれでいいのよ。\n前にも言った気がするけど、問題は、私:
"Thanks. But we're fine as we are.
I think I've said this before, but the problem is only on my end."
「鳥谷校長に対して、ずっと心の整理がついてなかった」: "For a long time I hadn't sorted out my feelings toward Headmaster Toritani."
「うーん……何かあったといえば、あったし、ないと言えばないし……\n別にはぐらか:
"Hmm... you could say something did, and you could say it didn't...
I'm not trying to dodge the question or anything, I'm not you, Kusanagi."
「たださ、きっと口に出して説明しちゃうと、\nそんな程度のことで？ って思われる:
"It's just that if I actually put it into words, it's the kind of trivial thing
that would make you think -- 'That's all?'"
「霧乃さんと一緒に校長室に行ったときのこと、覚えてる？\nあのときに、校長が言っ:
"Do you remember when I went to the headmaster's office with Kirino-san?
What the headmaster said then..."
独り言のように呟かれた言葉を、俺もよく覚えていた。: Those words, murmured almost like a soliloquy, I remembered well too.
鳥谷は、校長と霧乃さんのやりとりを、ずっと見つめていた。: Toritani had been watching the exchange between the headmaster and Kirino-san the whole time.
一言一句聞き漏らすまいと、息をするのも忘れて、瞬きも忘れて、\nずっと、ずっと:
Determined not to miss a single word, forgetting to breathe, forgetting even to blink,
for a long, long time --
「圭のことを愛してるんだって、すとんと胸に落ちた。\n理屈じゃなくて、心で納得で:
"It settled into my chest that she loves Kei.
Not as reasoning -- I understood it in my heart."
「そりゃ、いきなり母親とか言えないし、家に帰ろうとか考えないけどね。\nちょっと:
"Of course I can't suddenly call her Mother, and I'm not about to move back home.
I think of it as having gone independent a little earlier than most."
「そうだな。やっと肩の荷が下りたような顔してるぞ」: "Yeah. You look like a weight's finally come off your shoulders."
「そうね、そんな感じよ。正直すっきりしたわ」: "Right. That's about it. Honestly, I feel refreshed."
「霧乃さんのことも、麗華のことも解決したしなぁ」: "Things with Kirino-san and with Reika got resolved too."
「そうね、あとはムーア展に向けて邁進するのみって感じね」: "Right. All that's left is to press on toward the Moore Exhibition."
「あ、ところでさ。この後、すこし時間ある？」: "Oh, by the way. Do you have some time after this?"
鳥谷が気軽な感じを装って、俺に語りかける。: Toritani spoke to me with a casually feigned lightness.
「おお、あるぞ、いくらでも。何なら一晩中でもかまわない」: "Oh, I've got as much as you want. I don't mind staying up all night, even."
「ちょっ！ な、何言ってるのよ、私は別にそういうつもりで……！」: "Wha -- what are you saying?! I didn't mean it like --!"
「そういうつもりって何だよ。話がしたいんじゃないのか？\n鳥谷、前に言ってただろ:
"What do you mean, 'like that'? You want to talk, don't you?
Toritani -- you said it before, remember? That before long, you wanted me to hear all of it."
「う、うっさいわね！ 私だって恥ずかしければ顔くらい赤くなるわよ！」: "Q-quiet! Even I go red in the face when I'm embarrassed!"
「いや、俺は全然かまわないぞ。そういう素の鳥谷は大歓迎だ」: "No, I don't mind at all. That kind of unguarded Toritani is more than welcome."
「くっ……も、もう、今日はやっぱり帰って！ はい解散！」: "Ugh... you know what, go home already! Party dismissed!"
「やだーじゃないでしょっ、私が、話さないって言ったんだから、\n今日はこれで終わ: "Don't 'noooo' me! I said I wasn't going to talk, so we're done for today!"
「いいじゃないか。色々問題も解決して、すっきりさっぱりして、\n話したいことを話:
"Come on, isn't it fine? Everything's been sorted out, everyone's cleared their minds --
it's a fine night for saying the things you want to say."
「そうね。ここで意地を張っても、しょうがないか」: "Right. I suppose being stubborn here won't get me anywhere."
意地というか、甘えているように聞こえるんだが、今は言わないでおこう。\n話が一:
More like sulking than stubbornness, it sounded to me -- but I'll leave that unsaid for now.
The conversation isn't going anywhere.
「俺も、鳥谷が語ろうとしていることに興味がある。\n真剣に、知りたいと思っている:
"I'm interested in what you're trying to tell me too.
Seriously -- I want to know."
「たぶんすこしだけ、長くなると思うから」: "Because I think it'll take a little while."
幼い頃の記憶をたどると、\n決まって背中ばかりを思い出す。:
When I trace back my earliest memories,
what comes back to me are, without fail, glimpses of her back.
私も圭も、母に育てられたという記憶はない。: Neither I nor Kei have any memory of being raised by our mother.
母は、いつもとても忙しい人だった。: Mother was always a very busy person.
父親とは、母以上に、会うことは稀だった。\n彼は仕事や社交に夢中で、子育てには:
Our father -- we saw even less of him than of Mother.
He was absorbed in his work and his social life, and had no interest in child-rearing.
私たちは、父方の祖母や、乳母代わりのお手伝いさんに育てられることに\nなった。:
We ended up being raised by our paternal grandmother
and by housekeepers who served as our nursemaids.
圭は生まれてすぐに、中村家に預けられた。: Kei was placed with the Nakamura family soon after birth.
けれど、私と圭が異母姉弟であることは、物心つく頃から知っていた。: But that Kei and I were half-siblings by different mothers -- I knew that from about the time I first became aware of myself.
中村家は、人の出入りの多い家だった。: The Nakamura household saw many people coming and going.
親族、客人、お手伝いさん……心ない周囲の大人から、\n圭の立場がどんなものであ:
Relatives, guests, housekeepers... from the thoughtless adults around us,
Kei's position in the world was made plain to us,
indirectly and directly, again and again.
圭は、疎んじられ、馬鹿にされ、冷遇された。: Kei was shunned, mocked, and coldly treated.
しかし、私もまた、似たような境遇にあった。: But I, too, was in a similar situation.
私は中村家の長女ではなく、常に母の娘として扱われていた。: I was never treated as the eldest daughter of the Nakamura family; I was always treated as my mother's daughter.
母親が何か中村家にとって良くないことをしたのだということは、\n幼年期には、既:
That my mother had done something the Nakamura family found unforgivable --
even as a small child, I already vaguely understood it.
何もかも母が悪いのだと、\n何度、祖母から呪いのように聞かされたことだろう。:
It's all Mother's fault -- how many times, like a curse,
did I hear that from my grandmother?
お前は、あの女から生まれた事自体が罪なのだと、\n何度、小姑から聞かされたこと:
The very fact that you were born of that woman is your sin --
how many times did I hear that from my father's sister?
それでも、私達は、ほとんど顔も見ない母よりも、\n目の前の呪詛を吐く人間たちの:
And yet, more than the mother whose face we hardly ever saw,
it was the people right in front of us spitting their curses that we could not trust.
この人間たちの言葉よりも、何も言わないあの背中の方が、ずっと、\nなぜか、どう:
More than the words of these people, that silent back of hers seemed to us --
for some reason, somehow -- far, far more pure.
祖母や小姑には、可愛げのない子どもだと、なじられた。: An unlovable child, my grandmother and aunt would call me, and berate me.
私達は、あの家にあって常に孤独だった。: We were always alone in that house.
……母が、忙しいだけでなく、私たちから意図的に遠ざけられていたのだと\n知った:
...That my mother had been not merely busy but deliberately kept away from us --
I didn't come to know that until much later.
あまり幸福とは言えない幼少期ではあったが、長い歴史の中で多くの文化人や芸術家を: It was not a childhood one could call happy, but because the Nakamura family managed Yumihari Academy, which over its long history had produced many cultural figures and artists, the house was hung with many works of art, and those became our consolation.
幼い子どもである私たちにとっては、あまりにも広大な中村の屋敷を、\nふたり手を:
Small children as we were, we would explore the Nakamura estate -- far too vast for us --
hand in hand, and touch its many artworks.
沢山の絵に囲まれて、私達も自然に絵を描くようになっていた。: Surrounded by so many paintings, we naturally began to paint as well.
私達にほとんど無関心であった父は、\nなぜか絵を描くことだけには難色を示した。:
Our father, who was almost wholly indifferent to us,
for some reason showed reluctance about one thing alone: our painting.
どんなに嫌がっても、私達が絵を描くのをやめないとわかると、\nますます冷淡に、:
No matter how much he disliked it, once he realized we wouldn't stop painting,
he grew ever colder, ever more distant.
母は逆に協力的で、私たちが絵画教室に通えるように取り計らってくれた。: Mother, on the contrary, was cooperative, and arranged for us to attend a painting class.
絵画教室で絵を描く時間は、私達にとって、\n何も考えずに絵を楽しめる自由な時間:
The hours we spent painting at that class were, for us,
free hours when we could enjoy painting without thinking of anything.
私は、早く大人になりたかった。: I wanted to grow up quickly.
大人になって、この、澱みの中にあるような中村の家から、しがらみから、\n自由に:
I wished to grow up, and to be free of that Nakamura house that seemed to lie in stagnant water,
free of all its entanglements.
でも、私は大人になるよりも、もっとずっと早くに、\n中村家を出ることになった。:
But I ended up leaving the Nakamura house far, far sooner
than I ever grew up.
母は私の親権は獲得したが、圭は養子として夏目家に行くことになり、\n圭や私の描:
Mother won custody of me, but Kei was to go to the Natsume family as an adopted son,
and the paintings Kei and I had made were to be kept at the Toritani house.
――妾の子だから、圭は夏目家にいくのよ！: -- Because he's a mistress's child, that's why Kei goes to the Natsume house!
――お前の母親にとって、圭は不要なのよ！: -- For your mother, Kei is unwanted!
――絵は買い取っても、圭は買い取ってもらえなかったわね！: -- The paintings she bought back, but Kei -- Kei she wouldn't buy!
……あの時の麗華の言葉は、私の弱い部分に深く突き刺り、\n抜けない棘になった。:
...Reika's words that day pierced deep into the weakest part of me,
and became a thorn I could never pull out.
私はまだあまりにも幼く、\n圭だけが夏目家に行くことを理性で納得するのは、ひど:
I was still far too young,
and to accept with reason that only Kei was going to the Natsume family was terribly hard.
母は離婚後、さらに忙しくなった。: After the divorce, Mother grew even busier.
離婚後の煩雑な交渉や、校長の仕事、理事との折衝に忙殺され、\n私との時間をどう:
Swamped with the tangled negotiations following the divorce, with her duties as principal, with the mediations among the board members,
she simply could not find time for me.
母の離婚後、私は、母の実家である鳥谷の家で暮らすことになった。: After Mother's divorce, I came to live at the Toritani house, her family home.
鳥谷の祖父母は私を疎むこともなかったが、特に歓迎もしなかった。: My Toritani grandparents did not shun me, but neither did they especially welcome me.
ずっと一緒だった圭とも引き離され、慣れない家で私は独り、\n静かに鬱屈していっ:
Torn away from Kei, who had been with me all along, alone in a house I could not get used to,
I grew quietly, inwardly, more and more brooding.
そんな私を慰めてくれたのは、母方の年の離れた従姉妹だった。\n従姉妹の名前は、:
The one who consoled me then was a cousin on my mother's side, much older than I was.
Her name was Toritani Shizuru.
鳥谷の家に来るまで、存在も知らなかった従姉妹だが、\n頻繁に遊びに来る彼女の存:
Until I came to the Toritani house I hadn't even known she existed,
but through the presence of this cousin who visited often, my heart little by little softened.
私が境遇の割には比較的健全で、明るい人間に育ったのは、\n静流のおかげだろう。:
That I grew up relatively sound and cheerful, given my circumstances,
I owe, I think, to Shizuru.
「どうしてお母さんは、圭を引き取ってくれなかったんだろう」: "Why is it that Mother wouldn't take Kei in, I wonder?"
ある日、保管庫で圭の絵を見ながらつぶやいた私に、\n静流はこう答えてくれた。:
One day, when I murmured this while looking at Kei's paintings in the storeroom,
Shizuru answered me like this.
『あの人は、とても頭の良い人だから、そして優しい人だから、\nだからきっとなにか:
"That person is very clever, and very kind,
so surely there must be some reason."
私は、静流の優しさに感謝した。: I was grateful for Shizuru's kindness.
けれど私は、その頃にはもう、静流が言う母の優しさも、理由も、\n信じることがで:
But by then I had already lost the ability to believe in the kindness of Mother
that Shizuru spoke of, or in her reasons.
しばらくして、静流は趣味が高じたコーヒー修行のために海外に出た。: After a while, Shizuru went abroad to train in the art of coffee, a hobby that had grown into a calling.
私が彼女の一番の理解者で、一番の賛同者だった。\n私は、笑って手を振って、彼女:
I was her greatest understander, her greatest supporter.
Smiling, waving, I saw her off.
そしてまた私は、独りになった。: And once again, I was alone.
時々、鳥谷の家で会う母の口ぶりから、\n少しずつ状況が落ち着きつつあることは、:
From Mother's manner, on the occasions when I met her at the Toritani house,
I could tell that things were, little by little, settling down.
私達は、離れていた時間があまりにも長くなりすぎていた。: But the time we had spent apart had grown too long.
生まれてからずっと、母と話す機会は数えるほどしかなくて、\n私達はお互いに、ど:
From the moment I was born, I could count on my fingers the times we had spoken,
and neither of us any longer knew how to be, or should be, mother and daughter.
たまの二人での食事でも言葉は少なかった。\n向かいあっても、背中を向けられてい:
Even at our rare meals together, words were few.
Even face to face, I felt as though her back were turned to me.
「何か話したいことはある？」: "Is there anything you want to talk about?"
母からの言葉に、私はただ首を振った。: To Mother's words, I only shook my head.
話したくないわけではなかった。: It wasn't that I didn't want to talk.
聞きたいことが、ずっとあった。: There was something I had long, long wanted to ask.
――どうして、圭はこの家に来れなかったの。: -- Why couldn't Kei come to this house?
――圭は、いらない子だったの。: -- Was Kei a child you didn't want?
喉の奥で冷えて固まった疑問は、\n長い年月の間に、余りに大きくなりすぎていた。:
The question, cold and hardened in the back of my throat,
had, over the long years, grown far too large.
もし本当に、圭が妾の子だから夏目家に養子になったのだと言われたら\n私は母を憎:
If I were told that Kei really had been sent to the Natsume family because he was a mistress's child,
I might come to hate my mother.
それが恐ろしかった。\nそれでもまだ、母親だった。:
That was what I feared.
Even so, she was still my mother.
祖母は私に優しくもなく冷たくもなく、\nけれど、私の生活の世話を、きちんとして:
My grandmother had been neither kind nor cold to me,
but she had properly seen to the care of my daily life.
それで十分だった。感謝していた。: That was enough. I was grateful.
母は、祖母の臨終の席には間に合わなかった。: Mother did not arrive in time for her mother's deathbed.
亡くなった祖母の前に現れた母は、ひどく冷静だった。: When Mother appeared before her dead mother, she was terribly composed.
対面しても涙ひとつ見せず、\n部屋を出たところで、通夜と葬儀の手配について話し:
Facing her, she did not shed a single tear,
and as soon as she stepped out of the room, she began to talk about arrangements for the wake and funeral.
私の中で、何かが弾けた。\n激しい感情が奔流となって、私の口から溢れ出た。:
Something inside me snapped.
A violent surge of feeling came pouring out of my mouth.
私は、母をなじった。\nなんて酷い、冷たい人だと。:
I railed at Mother.
What a cruel, cold person she was.
母は何も言わず、じっと黙って聞いていた。: Mother said nothing, only listened in silence.
心の中に溜まりに溜まっていた母への恨みを、\n言葉にして全て叩きつけた。:
All the resentment I had bottled up inside toward her,
I hurled at her in words.
でも、それでも、圭の事は聞けなかった。: But even then, I could not bring myself to ask about Kei.
全てを吐き出し終えた私に、母は静かに告げた。: When I had spat it all out, Mother told me quietly,
「そうだ。私は冷たい人間だ」: "That's right. I am a cold person."
「事実、私は子どもよりも学園を優先させていた。\n姪に娘の面倒をまかせて、何もし:
"In fact, I put the school before my children.
I left my niece to look after my daughter, and did nothing myself."

シャルル・ペローの童話集は民間伝承を扱った物語集の中でも、最も古いものといって: Charles Perrault's collection of fairy tales may be called one of the oldest of all such collections dealing in folklore.

「何言ってるんだよ。直哉のご飯だったら食べるに決まってるじゃないか」: "What are you saying? If it's your cooking, Naoya, of course I'm going to eat it."
「ったく、お前は、そういうところが本当にキモイよな」: "Geez, that side of you is really creepy, you know."
「キモイとか言うな！ 怒るぞ！」: "Don't call me creepy! I'll get mad!"
いつもの口調で圭が怒った。: Kei snapped back in his usual tone.
「こんなところまで来るとはな……」: "To think you'd come all the way out here..."
夏目家の門をくぐると、あいつがいた。: When I passed through the gate of the Natsume estate, she was there.
「あの後、ずっと考えました」: "I've been thinking, ever since that day."
「『櫻七相図』が誰の作品であるかどうかです」: "About whose work 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura' truly is."
「だから、昨日、お前が見た通りだ。俺にあれを描く力は無い」: "Like I told you, you saw it yesterday. I don't have the ability to paint that."
「それは分かってます。あなたの腕がもう使い物にならない事も、\n草薙健一郎の筆を: "I understand that. I know your arm is useless now, and that reproducing Kusanagi Ken'ichirou's brushwork is impossible."
「ならば結論は出ているだろう」: "Then the conclusion is obvious, isn't it?"
「だったらどけ……遅刻する。\nお前だって登校しなきゃいけないんじゃないのか？」: "Then get out of the way... I'll be late. Don't you have to get to school too?"
「私の結論は……\n『櫻七相図』は、草薙直哉作です」: "My conclusion is... 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura' is the work of Kusanagi Naoya."

「草薙くんは、自分が描いた作品に対してなんの責任も持たないのですか？」: "Kusanagi-kun, do you bear no responsibility whatsoever for the works you've created?"
「はい、あの作品は間違いなく草薙直哉の作品です。\nですが、それをあなたは偽って: "Yes, that piece is unmistakably the work of Kusanagi Naoya. And yet you're lying about it."
「偽りの答えで満足する人間ならば、それで良いでしょう」: "If you're the sort of person who can be satisfied with a false answer, then fine."
「ですが、その偽りの答えでは満足しない人間だっているのです」: "But there are people who cannot be satisfied by that false answer."
「作品を作った人間は、作品に向けられた真なる問いに対して、偽りをもって答えて良い: "Does the one who made the work have the right to answer a true question posed to it with a lie?!"
俺は思わず目を伏せてしまう。: Without meaning to, I lowered my eyes.
「私は凡人です。凡人だからこそ、私は私の感覚を信じている」: "I am ordinary. Precisely because I am ordinary, I trust my own senses."
「だって、才能が偽物である私が、本物の芸術家の前に立つには、その目だけは、その感: "For someone like me, whose talent is counterfeit, to stand before a true artist, at least my eyes, at least my senses, have to be real."
「じゃなければ、私はこんなバカバカしい事なんてしていない」: "Otherwise I wouldn't be doing something this ridiculous."
「本物かどうか分からなければ、すぐにあきらめがつくんだ……」: "If I couldn't even tell the real from the fake, I could give up right away..."
「だからこそ、私は私が本物だと感じたものを信じる」: "That's exactly why I trust the things I feel to be real."
話では、子供の時に同じクラスだった事があるそうだ……。: Apparently we were in the same class once, when we were children...
こいつはその事を覚えているが、俺はその事をほとんど覚えていない。: She remembers it, but I barely do.
何故、こいつは俺にここまでこだわるのだろうか？: Why is she so fixated on me?
何故、つきまとうのだろう。: Why does she keep following me around?
「才能が無いのは同じだろ……。\n昨日見ただろ……」: "You have no talent either, do you...? You saw yesterday..."
「才能がないやつが、本物を見極める目を持っていたとしたら、\n簡単にあきらめるわ: "If someone with no talent possessed the eyes to discern the real thing, there's no way she could give up easily."

「だって、その事に価値を感じないから」: "Because you don't feel any value in it."
「でも、才能が無い人間は違う。\nその場所に手が届かないからこそあきらめない」: "But people without talent are different. Because they can't reach that place, they don't give up."

「それがとても価値のある事、自分の人生を捧げるのにふさわしい事を知っている」: "They know it's something of tremendous worth, something worth devoting an entire life to."
才能があるヤツはすぐにあきらめて。\n才能がないヤツはなかなかあきらめない。: Those with talent give up quickly. Those without don't give up easily.
実際、出来るヤツほど「こんなものか」と早々に見切りを付けてしまえる。\nつまり: In truth, the more capable someone is, the sooner they can write it off with a "so this is all it is." Which means they can give up easily, throw it away easily.
才能というのは厄介なもので、ありすぎると、その事に呑み込まれてしまう。: Talent is a troublesome thing -- too much of it, and you get swallowed by it.
才能がある故に、価値観を形成する前に、簡単な結果を出せてしまう。: Because you have talent, you can produce easy results before your sense of values has even taken shape.
だから、すぐにあきらめる事が出来る。: And so you can give up right away.
こいつはそういう事を言っているのだろう。: That must be what she's saying.
「まず、訂正させてもらうが、俺は簡単にあきらめてなどいない」: "First, let me correct you. I haven't given up so easily."
「あとな、見る目があるヤツは才能が無いとは言わないよ」: "And another thing -- you don't say someone with a discerning eye has no talent."
「それだけでも大層な才能だ。お前には才能がある」: "That alone is a considerable talent. You have talent."
「お世辞ですか？ そんなお世辞で喜ぶほど、私の人生は甘くありませんでした」: "Flattery? My life hasn't been sweet enough that I'd rejoice at that kind of flattery."
「なんで、そうなるんだよ……」: "Why does it come out that way..."
「本物が分かる目など、この世を生きていて苦痛でしかありません。\n他の連中みたい: "Having eyes that can see the real thing is nothing but suffering in this world. It'd be far happier to be like the others, getting excited over garbage."
「世の中の連中。全員幸せそうじゃないですか。\n何故だと思いますか？ やつらには: "The people out there in the world -- every one of them looks happy, don't they? Why do you think that is? Because they can't tell fake from real."
「やつらに分かるのは、他の大多数が喜んでいるかどうかだけ。\n空気を読む力だけ」: "All they can tell is whether the majority of others are pleased. Just the power to read the mood."

「それでも、価値の無い物を作り出す人間どもに、おもねる事なんて出来ない」: "Even so, I can't bring myself to pander to those who churn out worthless things."
「けど、けどですね。\n私の戦いなど、いつも負けばかりです……」: "But, but you see. My battles are always nothing but losses..."
「価値が分かるなんて事は何の力でもないんです。\n価値を自ら作り出さなければ、そ: "Being able to recognize value isn't a power at all. Unless you can create value yourself, it means nothing."
「自分で価値が作り出せない芸術家など、存在しないも同じです」: "An artist who can't produce value on his own may as well not exist."
「お前がそう思うのなら、そうなのだろ……」: "If that's what you think, then I guess that's how it is..."
「はい、私はそう信じている。\nだから、私は私の信念によってしか動かない」: "Yes, that's what I believe. And so I move only according to my convictions."
「それが、正しいかどうかなんて知った事じゃない」: "Whether that's right or wrong is no concern of mine."
「もしそれが、後ろ指さされる行為だとしても、軽蔑される様な行為だとしても、私は私: "Even if it's something people would point fingers at, even if it's something contemptible, I'll do anything to give birth to my own value."
「私は、平気で他人を陥れるし、嘘だってつくし、その他のあらゆる事だって出来る」: "I'll gladly frame others, I'll lie, I'll do anything else you can name."
「私は、私の芸術を一番愛している」: "I love my art more than anything."
「そうかい、おぞましいほどの情熱だな……」: "I see. A frightful sort of passion..."
「んで？ そんなヤツが何故、ジャンクである俺なんかにつきまとう。\nもう意味なん: "So then? Why does someone like that keep hounding a piece of junk like me? There's no point anymore, is there?"
「私が前に進むためには、どうあってもあなたと『櫻七相図』の真実だけは知らなければ: "In order for me to move forward, no matter what, I have to know the truth of you and 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura.'"
「あなたがどんな嘘をつこうと、私は諦めない」: "No matter what lies you tell, I won't give up."
「私はどこまでもあなたにつきまとうわ！」: "I'll follow you to the ends of the earth!"
もともと一癖も二癖もあるヤツだと思っていたが……こんな目で見られるとはな……。: I'd figured from the start she was a piece of work -- but to be looked at with eyes like these...
「とんだヤツに目を付けられた……」: "A hell of a person's got her eye on me..."
「それでも、お前がお前の価値のために戦うのは分かった。\nんで？ それと俺の絵が: "Still, I get that you fight for your own value. So? What does that have to do with my paintings?"
「私は、あなたの才能によって、自分自身を思い知らされた」: "Your talent made me realize what I truly am."
「だから、あなたが筆を折った事には感謝している」: "So I'm grateful you broke your brush."

「何言ってるんだよ。創作をやってる人間なら少しは思う事だよ。\nま、そんな堂々と: "What are you talking about. Anyone who does creative work has felt that a little. Though someone who says it so openly is rare."
「それでもあなたは再び描いた。\nあの右腕を失っても、あなたは描ききった」: "And yet you painted again. Even having lost that right arm, you painted it through to the end."
「迷惑な話だ……。正直、お前が前に進もうと、止まろうと、俺には知った事じゃないけ: "How inconvenient... Honestly, whether you move forward or stand still is none of my business..."
「そうでしょうね。でも、私もあなたがどんなに拒否しても、その真相にたどり着く」: "I imagine so. But no matter how much you refuse, I'll reach that truth."
「お前は、自分をどう思っているか知らないが、\n作品を生み出す苦しさを知る人間な: "I don't know what you think of yourself, but anyone who knows the pain of bringing a work into being isn't going to lightly despise someone like you."
「お前を軽蔑する人間は、その苦しさを知らない連中ばかりだろう……」: "The ones who despise you are all people who don't know that pain..."
「むしろ、俺は、それほど真っ直ぐなお前に感服するぐらいだ……」: "If anything, I'm almost impressed by how straightforward you are..."
「だから、見ていくか？ お前が探していた真相とやらを？」: "So, want to see it? That truth you've been searching for?"
「嘘なんて言わねぇよ……。アトリエはこっちだ……」: "I wouldn't lie about it... The atelier is this way..."
「ただ、すげぇつまんない結果で、愕然とする事請け合いだぞ」: "Just a warning -- the result is dreadfully dull. You'll be stunned by how unremarkable it is."
「真実なんてもんは、案外つまらないものだ……」: "The truth, as it turns out, is often surprisingly boring..."
俺は夏目の屋敷の門を戻る。: I turned back through the gate of the Natsume estate.
本来ならば、他人に明かして良い様な事ではない。: Normally this isn't something to reveal to others.
贋作制作の手法など、こんなヤツに教えるなどもってのほかだ……。\nだが、何故か: Teaching someone like her the technique for producing a forgery is out of the question... And yet, for some reason, I felt I had to show it to her.
その理由は自分でも良く分からない。: Even I don't really understand why.
昨晩から、蔵は俺専用のアトリエになっている。: Since last night, the storehouse has become my personal atelier.
もちろん、その専用にはあれも含まれている。: Of course, "personal" includes that as well.
「なんですか？ これ……これって……………スプリング？」: "What is this? This is... a spring?"
「そうだ。スプリングだ。身体を鍛えるやつだな」: "That's right. A spring. The kind used for muscle training."
「それを四方に張って、まん中に異様に長い筆……これって、もしかして」: "Stretched to the four sides, with a strangely long brush at the center... could this be--"
「草薙健一郎はとてつもなく長い筆を使った事で知られている。\n長い筆は、指の小さ: "Kusanagi Ken'ichirou is known for using an extraordinarily long brush. A long brush lets you draw a large, clean stroke from a small movement of the fingers."
「ああ、俺もガキの頃はこの筆を使って、延々と○だけを描かされたよ。\n基本的に世: "Yeah, when I was a kid I was made to use this brush and endlessly draw nothing but circles. Fundamentally the world is made of circles, triangles, and squares. The idea is that if you can draw those cleanly, you've built the foundation."
「コンパスを使った様な円、この筆を持たされて、まず課された課題がそれだった。幼少: "A circle like it was drawn with a compass -- that was the first task assigned to me once I was handed this brush. In early childhood I drew nothing but circles for hours every day. That was fairly hard."
「幼少期に……延々と円だけ描かされるなんて……過酷な子供時代ですね」: "In early childhood... being made to draw only circles, endlessly... what a harsh childhood."
「おかげで、一メートルほどの円ならば、ほぼ誤差なし、コンパス並だ」: "Thanks to it, a circle of about a meter comes out with almost no error, on par with a compass."
「それが出来る頃には、筆が届く範囲ならば、自由自在に曲線を描き分ける事が出来る様: "By the time I could do that, I could freely draw any curve within reach of the brush."
「曲線の中でも真円が精度的には一番難しいからな」: "Among curves, a true circle is the hardest in terms of precision."
「長い筆はどんな巨大なキャンバスにも美しい線をおとす」: "A long brush lays down beautiful lines on any canvas, however huge."
「綺麗な曲線は絵描きにとっては強い武器だ」: "Clean curves are a powerful weapon for a painter."
「ただし、この筆を使えば分かるが、それには、まったくぶれない筋力が必要となる。震: "That said, once you use this brush, you'll understand -- it demands absolutely unwavering muscle. An arm that doesn't tremble, doesn't move, and keeps the hand perfectly level."
「とてつもない筋力と、そして独特な感覚が必要とされる」: "It requires tremendous physical strength, and a peculiar sense besides."
「それが、草薙健一郎の線の秘密」: "That is the secret of Kusanagi Ken'ichirou's line."
「そして、このスプリングが、その筆質を再現する装置。\nこの装置を使ったからこそ: "And this spring is the device that reproduces the quality of his brushstrokes. It's because he used this device that that piece was painted..."
「ご明察だ。これが『櫻七相図』の真相ってやつだ」: "Well observed. This is what you'd call the truth of 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura.'"
「なるほど、だったら全然ジャンクじゃない。それで草薙直哉は描き続ければいいのだか: "I see. Then it isn't junk at all. Kusanagi Naoya just has to keep painting."
「そう思うよな。昨晩から描いているが……見ていくか？」: "That's what you'd think. I've been painting since last night... want to watch?"
「ここまで見せたのだからな。\nそいつを見て、是非とも二度と俺に対する興味を失っ: "I've shown you this much already. Watch it, and please, by all means, lose all interest in me for good."
おれは巨大なキャンバスを立てかける。: I set up the enormous canvas.
昨晩から作業をしているものだ。: The one I'd been working on since last night.
作業開始してから二時間ほど、普通ならば他人の作業など見ていたら飽きるだろうに、: About two hours in -- ordinarily anyone would get bored watching someone else work -- Nagayama watched what I was doing with devouring intensity.
「たしかに筆質は再現されています」: "The quality of the strokes is certainly reproduced."
「でも……これは、それ以上のものではない……」: "But... this is nothing more than that..."
「さすがに、本物が分かると自負しているだけはある」: "Fair enough -- you really do have the eye to know the real thing, just as you claim."
数時間かけて形成されていく習作。: A study piece forming over the course of several hours.
だが、その習作に筆を入れるたびに、凡庸性がきわまっていく。: But with every stroke laid on it, its mediocrity only deepens.
「櫻七相図を描いた時は、何かしら……」: "When I painted 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura,' there was something..."
「霊的？ そう言ってもいいかもしれない。\n描けるという直感があった」:
"Spiritual, maybe? You could call it that.
I had the intuition that I could paint it."
「だが、今はこの通りだ」: "But now, this is what it looks like."

「そうだな、一年も経ってない」: "That's true. It hasn't even been a year."
「たった一年で才能が枯渇するものでしょうか？」: "Can talent really run dry in just a single year?"
「あるいは、数年ぶりの作品だったので、七相図にはアイディアのストックがあったのか: "Or perhaps, since it was my first work in years, I had a stockpile of ideas saved up for the Seven Aspects."
「描かなかった六年間の集大成とも言える」: "You could call it the culmination of the six years I spent not painting."
「だから俺の才能は、七相図六部作、これによってすべてを使い切ったという見方も出来: "So one way to see it is that my talent was entirely spent on the six pieces of the Seven Aspects..."
「どちらにしても、今の俺はこんなもんだ」: "Either way, this is what I amount to now."
長山はその場で考え込む。: Nagayama stood there deep in thought.
無言の時間が十数分ほど続いた。: The silence went on for more than ten minutes.
すると、長山の重い口がやっとひらく。: And then, at last, Nagayama's heavy lips parted.
感想のたぐいではなく、ただの礼。: Not a response of any sort, just plain thanks.
まぁ、これを見せられて口に出来る言葉など、そんなものだろう。: Well, having been shown all this, that's probably about all one can say.
「いやいや、礼ならいいさ。\nそれよりも、櫻七相図の件は当然秘密にしてほしい」:
"No, no, no thanks needed.

「ああ、中村家というヤクザの様な連中が関わる問題だ。\nうかつに入り込まない方が: "Yeah. The Nakamura family -- they're basically yakuza. Better not to get carelessly involved."

言わぬ方が長山的にも得策であろう。: Keeping quiet was the wiser move for Nagayama as well.
「ふむ、では遅刻となったが、俺はそろそろ学校に行く」: "Well then, late as I am, I should be heading to school."
「そうですね。それが良いでしょう……」: "Yes. That would be for the best..."
今の俺の事実をどう受け止めるべきか分からないのだろうか？\nだが、どちらにして:
Perhaps she didn't know how she was supposed to take the truth of what I am now.
