「国境を越える唯一の蝶と言われております」: "It's said to be the only butterfly that crosses national borders."
「しかし、すごいですねぇ。いや、さっきからすごいしか言ってなくて、まったく司会者: "It really is amazing, isn't it. Ah, I've been saying nothing but 'amazing' -- I'm entirely failing as an emcee..."
「なんといいましょうか……幻想的な蝶の群れ、そして手前のうずしお……これが、私な: "How can I put it... this fantastical swarm of butterflies, and the whirlpool in the foreground... for someone like me, it evokes death."
「一匹として、うずしおに蝶がのまれているわけではないのですが……なんといいますか: "Not a single butterfly has been swallowed by the whirlpool, and yet... how should I say it... though none are being swallowed, it feels as though they might be..."
そう計算されて描かれている。: It's painted with that in mind, calculated.
空を埋め尽くす優雅な蝶と、うねる透明な海と強調されて描かれたうずしお。: Elegant butterflies filling the sky, and a rolling transparent sea with the whirlpool rendered in emphatic detail.
まるでそれぞれが別世界で起きている様でありながら、一つの世界に表現する事によっ: They look almost as though each were occurring in a separate world, yet by expressing them within a single world, the painting gives the viewer a strong sense of dissonance.
その違和感は不安を想起させるが、その不安が奥に描かれる美しい蝶の群れによって相: That dissonance evokes unease, but that unease is counterbalanced by the beautiful swarm of butterflies painted in the distance.
意識が美しさを、無意識が恐怖を感じる。\nその様な混乱を見る者に与える様に計算:
The conscious mind feels beauty; the unconscious feels dread.
It's calculated to inflict that kind of confusion on the viewer.
『櫻七相図』はあえて死骸を描く事によって死を表現。: 'The Seven Aspects of the Sakura' expresses death by daring to paint the corpse.
だが、『蝶を夢む』は死を一切描かない事によって、死を表現した。: But 'Dreaming of Butterflies' expresses death by not painting death at all.
もちろん、それが完全に成功しているかどうかは分からなかった。: Of course, I couldn't tell whether that had entirely succeeded.
だが、この感触。\n間違いなく俺の意図は成功した。:
But this feeling in the room --
there was no doubt: my intention had gotten through.
「この感覚……なんとも言えませんね。\nこれは日本画なのですか？」:
"This sensation... I can hardly put it into words.
Is this a nihonga -- a traditional Japanese-style painting?"
「はい、あえてその様な作品にしました」: "Yes. I deliberately made it that kind of work."
日本画家、速水御舟に有名な絵画がある。\n『炎舞』:
Among nihonga painters, Hayami Gyoshuu has a famous painting.
'Enbu' -- 'Dance of Flames.'
まさに焚き火に焼かれんばかりの蛾を描いた作品だ。: It depicts moths that look about to be consumed by a bonfire.
速水御舟は、毎晩焚き火をたき、そこに群がる蛾を実際に写生したと言われている。: Hayami Gyoshuu is said to have lit a bonfire every night and sketched the moths that gathered to it from life.
炎は仏画で使われる独特の紅蓮の炎。: The flames are the distinctive crimson lotus fire used in Buddhist paintings.
その上空を舞う蛾の姿。: Above them, the figures of the moths dancing.
この美しさをあえてすべて逆の方向で表現した。: I dared to express that beauty by taking the opposite approach in every respect.
仏教の様なデフォルメされた炎ではなく、あくまでも写実的でありながらも日本画らし: Not a Buddhist-style deformed fire, but a rendering of sea and whirlpool that is thoroughly realistic and yet still distinctly nihonga (if someone were to say it looked like Okumura Togyuu, well, that's exactly right).
そして蛾ではなく、美しい蝶の群れ。: And not moths, but a swarm of beautiful butterflies.
構図、作品性、技法、どれをとっても俺が描いた今までの絵を遙かに凌駕する出来だ。: Composition, thematic depth, technique -- by any measure, it's a work that far surpasses anything I've painted before.
「これは古典的かつストレートな日本画ですねぇ。今までの作品がポップアートなどの現: "This is a classic, straightforward piece of nihonga. Your previous work has centered on pop art and other contemporary art, so this comes as a bit of a surprise."
「しかし、これほどの日本画ならば、さぞ高名な日本画の師に教わったのでは？」: "But for a nihonga of this caliber, you must have studied under some prominent nihonga master?"
「いや、教わったのは父、草薙健一郎のみです。あとは独学です」: "No, the only person I studied under was my father, Kusanagi Ken'ichirou. The rest was self-taught."
「たしかに、草薙健一郎氏は日本画も描かれてましたが、それにしてもここまでの作品を: "True, Kusanagi Ken'ichirou-shi did paint nihonga as well, but even so, to produce a work of this level at such a young age..."
その後も話は続いたが、俺が説明する事はその程度だった。: The conversation went on after that, but that was about all I had to explain.
あらためて自分の絵を見てみる。: I looked again at my own painting.
いや、むしろ、我ながら良く描けている。: No -- if I say so myself, it's well done.
最高傑作と言って問題ない。: I have no problem calling it my finest work.
俺が出来うる限りの最高の作品だ！: The best work I could possibly produce!
俺が席に戻ると、何故か横の男にヘッドロックされる。: When I returned to my seat, for some reason the man next to me put me in a headlock.
「てめぇ、とんでもないもん描いてくれるじゃねぇかよぉぉ」: "You little bastard, painting something outrageous like thaaat..."
「だ、だからって、ヘッドロックはないでしょう」: "E-even so, a headlock's a bit much, isn't it?"
「ふふふ、案外、坂本は草薙くんに負けるかもしれないね」: "Heheh -- surprisingly, Sakamoto, you might lose to Kusanagi-kun."
「いや、そんな事はない。俺はアレだよ。俺はすごいもん」: "No, that's not going to happen. I'm, you know. I'm impressive too."
「だ、だったらヘッドロックするのやめてもらえませんか？」: "Th-then could you please stop the headlock?"
「少し、伝統的すぎるとも言えるが……、いや、それを逆手に取った様な素晴らしい作品: "You could argue it's a touch too traditional... but no, it's a wonderful work that turns that very traditionalism to its advantage."
「草薙健一郎も現代アートの路線から、いきなり『横たわる櫻』の様な伝統的な技法の作: "Kusanagi Ken'ichirou, too, suddenly shifted from the contemporary art track to painting a traditional-technique work like 'The Reclining Sakura.'"
「さて、それでは最後の作品です。最後の作品は……夏目圭氏作」: "Now then, the final work. The last piece is... by Natsume Kei-shi."
やつが命を削って描いた絵が見られる。: I get to see the painting he shaved away his life to produce.
さぁ、圭、お前はどんな絵を描いた！: Come on, Kei -- what kind of painting did you make!
俺は心の中で問いかけた。: I asked it in my heart.
スポットライトが落ち、一枚の絵が浮かび上がる。: The spotlight dropped, and a single painting rose out of the dark.
ただ、一枚の絵だけ、壇上に浮かび上がる。: Only a single painting stood illuminated on the stage.
まったくの単純な二本の向日葵の絵だ。: It was an utterly simple painting of two sunflowers.
向日葵というモチーフ自体も、とてもありふれたものだ。: Even the motif itself, sunflowers, was extremely commonplace.
だが、壇上に咲いた向日葵は、今まで何処で見た向日葵とも違った。: And yet the sunflowers blooming on that stage were unlike any sunflowers I had ever seen anywhere.
ただそれだけなのに……絶対的な説得力があった。: That was all... and yet it carried an absolute, overwhelming conviction.
いや、あれは黄色ではなく赤なのか？: No -- was it not yellow, but red?
だが、それは、こちらに迫り来る様な強烈な印象を与える。\n燃えている様な、狂っ:
And yet they gave a fierce impression of pressing forward at the viewer.
As if burning, as if mad...
揺らめいている様であり、不動である様であり。柔らかそうであり、鉄の様に鋭そうで: As if wavering, as if immovable. Soft-looking, and sharp as iron; blood dripping down, and frozen in a single instant...
真逆の印象が強く、画面を拮抗している。: Diametrically opposite impressions held the picture plane in taut equilibrium.
それが見る者の視線に緊張感を与える。: That put a tension into the eye of whoever looked at it.
どの様な技法によって、そう見えるんだ？: What kind of technique made it appear like that?
いや、それを言ったら、間違いなく、構図、作品性、技法、どれをとっても俺が描いた: No -- if it came down to that, then without question, in composition, in artistic depth, in technique, in every measure, my 'Dreaming of Butterflies' was superior.
技法の問題ではない。: It wasn't a matter of technique.
端的にヤツの絵は凄かった。: Simply put, his painting was staggering.
俺は手を握りしめていた。血がにじみ出るほど……、: My hand was clenched tight. Tight enough for blood to bead up...
あいつの絵の様に、捉えようのない感情が俺を包み込む。: Like his painting itself, an emotion I couldn't grasp was wrapping itself around me.
圭の作品がすぐれている事は予想していた。: I had expected Kei's work to be excellent.
だが、この様な作品が俺の心をわしづかみするとは思ってもいなかった。: But I had never imagined a work like this would seize hold of my heart.
「誰だよ。あの夏目圭ってヤツ」: "Who the hell is he. This Natsume Kei guy."
「さぁな。どこかしら派閥の隠し球かもな。あんな絵描くヤツが今日まで無名とかありえ: "Beats me. Maybe some faction's hidden card. There's no way someone who paints like that could stay unknown until today."
「しかも作者不在かよ……」: "And on top of that, the artist isn't even here..."
「……うーん、難しい絵だなぁ。あれ、たぶん素人には落書きに見えるぞ」: "...Hmm, it's a difficult painting. To an amateur, that thing probably just looks like a scribble."
「それはどうかな……、逆に我々芸術家だからこそ難しく見えるのかもしれないぞ……」: "I wonder about that... on the contrary, it may be precisely because we're artists that it looks difficult to us..."
会場はシーンとしている。: The hall had gone dead silent.
誰もが、圭の絵に見入っていた。: Everyone was drawn into Kei's painting.
「難しいのなら、観客は動揺するハズだ。\nざわめきが聞こえるはずだ」:
"If it were difficult, the audience would be unsettled.
You'd hear a stir."
「だが、この静けさ……魅入られているのさ。あの絵に」: "But this stillness... they're enchanted. By that painting."
「印象派が出た時、あらゆる権威がこれを否定した」: "When the Impressionists appeared, every authority denied them."
「サロンと印象派が対立する様な構図の痕跡はいまだに見られる」: "The traces of that Salon-vs.-Impressionist opposition can still be seen even now."
「印象派の作品の多くがアメリカに流れたって事か？」: "You mean how most Impressionist works ended up flowing to America?"
「いいや、何故、フランスにはルーヴル美術館とオルセー美術館があるかって事だよ」: "No, I mean the reason France has both the Louvre and the Musee d'Orsay."
「サロンと対立した印象派の絵画はルーヴルではなくオルセーに飾られている」: "The Impressionist paintings that opposed the Salon aren't hung in the Louvre -- they're hung in the Orsay."
「元々はジュ・ド・ポーム国立美術館だけどな。まぁ言わんとする事は分かるよ」: "Originally at the Jeu de Paume, technically. But I get what you're saying."
「印象派を支持したのは他ならぬパリ市民だった」: "It was none other than the citizens of Paris who supported the Impressionists."
「今だと難解に見える印象派だが、当時のパリの人間には、それまでの芸術よりもよっぽ: "Impressionism looks difficult now, but for Parisians of the time, it was far more accessible, far more familiar, than the art that had come before."
「まぁ、印象派がジャポニスム……浮世絵などの影響が強い事も関連しているだろうな」: "Well, that Impressionism was strongly influenced by Japonisme -- ukiyo-e and the like -- probably has something to do with it."
「村田はあの夏目とやらの作品をえらく高く評価するのだな」: "You rate this Natsume fellow's work awfully highly, Murata."
「俺は、絵単体だと草薙ジュニアの方がすぐれていると思うがな」: "As a painting on its own, I still think Kusanagi Junior's is the better piece."
「まぁ、画家ならそう言うだろうな。だがムーアはどう判断するだろうか、あの絵を」: "Well, any painter would say so. But how will Moore judge that painting, I wonder."
「おいおい、あれに負けるの、いまいち納得いかないぞ」: "Come on -- I'm not entirely on board with losing to that."
俺はまるで魂が抜けてしまったかの様であった。: It was as if my very soul had been drained out of me.
負ける要素など無かった。: There was no element on which I should have lost.
実際、すべての要素で、俺は圭を上回っていただろう。: In fact, in every element, I surely surpassed Kei.
だが、作品というのはそういうものでは無い。: But that isn't what a work of art comes down to.
圭の色彩？ それとも筆遣い？ いやあの独特な構図？: Was it Kei's coloring? His brushwork? Or that peculiar composition?
いくら、分析してみても分からない。: No matter how I analyzed it, I couldn't understand.
分からないが、圭の絵は、人の心を打つ物であった。: I couldn't understand -- but Kei's painting was something that struck people to the heart.
司会者がしゃべっている間も会場は無音に包まれていた。: Even while the emcee was speaking, the hall remained enveloped in silence.
間違いなく会場の心を今日、一番掴んだ絵画。: Without question, the painting that had seized the hearts of the hall most today.
魂が抜けた様な俺など、誰も気にする事もなく、ムーア公募展は続いていた。: With no one paying any mind to me sitting there like a hollow shell, the Moore Open Exhibition went on.
どのぐらいの時間が経っただろうか？: How much time had passed, I wonder?
気がつくと授賞式になっていた。: When I came to myself, the award ceremony was under way.
「それでは栄えある、エラン・フォク賞は」: "And so, the honored Elan Foc prize goes to --"
「数々の世界的賞も獲得している。ポップアートの雄、村田清彦氏です」: "A winner of numerous world-class awards. The champion of pop art -- Murata Kiyohiko-shi."
盛大な拍手がわき起こる。: A grand round of applause welled up.
村田清彦氏が壇上に上がる。: Murata Kiyohiko-shi stepped up onto the stage.
本人も事前に知らされていたためか、非常に落ち着いている。: Perhaps because he'd been notified in advance, he was extraordinarily composed.
彼はこの賞を受賞する前からすでに世界的芸術家だ。: He was already a world-class artist even before receiving this prize.
だから、大本命。: So he'd been the overwhelming favorite.
三年ぶりの国内受賞者が彼だとしても、\n周囲にそれほどの驚きはない。:
Even if he was the first domestic winner in three years,
there was no great surprise around him.
報道陣のフラッシュが半端無い。: The flashes from the press corps were relentless.
村田清彦氏の作品はいつものタッチの作品であった。: Murata Kiyohiko-shi's work was in his usual style.
彼の作風は長らく海外でも浸透しており、今回の受賞は、この作品というよりは、今ま: His style had long since taken root overseas as well, and this award was less for this particular piece than a recognition of his career to date.
村田清彦氏の絵は元々かなり高値で取引されていたが、これでさらに値段がつり上がる: Murata Kiyohiko-shi's paintings had been trading at fairly high prices to begin with, but with this the prices would climb further.
今後は億単位の作品も売買されるかもしれない。: From here on, works of his might well change hands in the hundreds of millions.
ムーア公募展の受賞というのはそういうものだ。: That's the kind of thing winning the Moore Open Exhibition means.
華々しい舞台とは裏腹に、ノミネート作家の席に緊張が走る。: In contrast to the dazzling stage, tension ran through the seats of the nominated artists.
エラン・フォクはすでに情報が流出し村田氏に内定していた。: Word had already leaked that the Elan Foc had been unofficially decided for Murata-shi.
だが、もう一つあると言われている賞に関しては、ここにいる誰も知らされていないら: But as for the other prize said to be forthcoming, apparently no one here had been told a thing.
いやがおうにも空気がぴりぴりする。: Whether one liked it or not, the air prickled.
だが、そんな答えなど、俺にはどうでも良かった。: But for me, that answer didn't matter one way or the other.
あるいは、俺の中では決まり切っていたのかもしれない。: Or rather, within me, it may already have been entirely settled.
「今回はなんと、エラン・フォク賞以外にも、国内で受賞者がいるとの事ですよね」: "This time, in addition to the Elan Foc prize, we understand there's another domestic winner as well, isn't there?"
「そうですね。すでに世界同時発表で、エラン・ルートル、エラン・フォクの受賞者の名: "That's right. In the simultaneous worldwide announcement, the names of the winners of the Elan Loutre and the Elan Foc have already been released."
「そうすると、本日発表する、最後は、あのエラン・オタリとなります」: "Which means the final one to be announced today is that celebrated Elan Otarie."
「エラン・オタリといえば六年前に、篠山龍氏が受賞して以来、六年ぶりとなります」: "The Elan Otarie -- for the first time in six years, since Shinoyama Ryuu-shi received it six years ago."
「この賞は、世界でただ一人しか受け取れないという非常に貴重な賞です。\nそれまで:
"This is an exceptionally rare prize, awarded to only one person in the entire world.
It's said to go to someone whose talent promises still greater achievements to come, more than for their existing record in the art world."
「私達も誰だか知らされてません。はたして、この名誉な賞を受け取るのは誰でしょうか: "Even we haven't been told who it is. Just who will receive this honored prize?"
そして司会者は封を切り、中身を確認する。: Then the emcee broke the seal and checked the contents.
その後、少しの余韻を持たせて、司会者がその名を呼ぶ。: After that, letting the moment linger a beat, the emcee called out the name.
鳥谷の声だ。\n稟の声も聞こえる。:
That was Toritani's voice.
And I could hear Rin's voice too.
俺はその場で俯く。: I bowed my head where I sat.
いや、あの絵を見た瞬間に、この結果は分かっていた。: No -- the moment I had seen that painting, I had known this would be the result.
あの絵は、そういう絵だ。: That painting was that kind of painting.
「しかし、驚きましたねぇ。今まで世界的な実績がある人物だけが受賞してきたムーア公: "But what a surprise. The Moore Open Exhibition has, until now, been awarded only to figures with international track records, and to think a boy in his teens would win it -- of course, this sets a record for youngest recipient in its history..."
「歴史的な快挙としか言いようがありませんね。\nですが、こちらもちゃんとムーア財:
"There's no other way to describe it than a historic feat.
But here too, the Moore Foundation has attached a written explanation of the reasoning behind the award."
「エラン・オタリは年に一度、たった一人しか受賞出来ない賞ですが、あらゆる賞の中で: "The Elan Otarie can be awarded to only one person per year, and of all their prizes, it carries the strongest connotation of a rookie award."
「とは言うものの、今日まで、実績がほぼない少年が受賞する事などまったくありません: "That said, until today, it had essentially never gone to a boy with virtually no track record. As a rule, it was given to an artist who, though active internationally, remained unknown."
「ですが、今回は、ほぼ実績もなく、ただ一作品だけでの受賞という異例な事態になりま: "But this time, we have the exceptional situation of a win with practically no prior record, on the strength of just a single work."
フリッドマンが壇上に立つ。: Friedman stepped up onto the stage.
フリッドマンは何故か俺を見つめる。: For some reason, Friedman fixed his gaze on me.
「日本の芸術界は長らく閉鎖的であった」: "The Japanese art world has long been closed off."
「長らく、長らく、世界と断絶していたと言えます」: "For a long, long time, one could say it was cut off from the world."
「であるならば、この国は芸術不毛地帯であるのか？」: "If so -- is this country a barren wasteland for art?"

「葛飾北斎。ヒロシゲブルーと賞された歌川広重。歌川国芳。喜多川歌麿……ここで名前: "Katsushika Hokusai. Utagawa Hiroshige, praised for his 'Hiroshige blue.' Utagawa Kuniyoshi. Kitagawa Utamaro... just naming them here would eat up all our time."
「芸術に愛された土地と言って良いでしょう。\n少なくとも、多くの印象派の画家達は:
"One may safely call it a land beloved of art.
At the very least, many of the Impressionist painters believed as much without question."
「多くの工芸品もまた世界中で愛され珍重されている」: "Many of its crafts, too, are loved and prized the world over."
「王室御用達であったロイヤルコペンハーゲンは、古くから日本の古伊万里染付の影響を: "Royal Copenhagen, purveyor to the Danish court, is well known to have been strongly influenced from long ago by Japan's ko-Imari blue-and-white porcelain."
「ここは芸術不毛どころか、オルタナティブな芸術が生まれる地であるのです」: "Far from being barren of art, this is a land where alternative art is born."
「ですがオルタナティブ故に、この地は欧米芸術と隔離された状況に長らくありました」: "But precisely because it is alternative, this land was long kept in isolation from Western art."
「草薙健一郎氏が受賞してから六年」: "Six years since Kusanagi Ken'ichirou-shi received his award."
「この地は、ふたたび欧米と合流した」: "This land has, once again, rejoined the West."
「違った道を歩んだ芸術が、また再会したのです」: "Arts that had walked separate paths have met once more."
「それは、その後、ムーアにおける日本人受賞者の増加という形に現れています」: "That has since manifested in the form of an increase in Japanese laureates at the Moore."
「まさに、今、芸術が国境を無くして新たなるうねりを生みだそうとしている」: "Truly, right now, art is erasing its borders and about to give rise to a new surge."

「こうやって、寝っ転がって桜見るときれいですね」: "Lying down like this to watch the cherry blossoms, isn't it beautiful?"
「地上の底から、空を見上げる、地に落ちた桜の花弁が何度も舞い上がる……」: "Looking up at the sky from the bottom of the earth, and the fallen petals soaring up again and again......"
「いつだったか、ここで圭とこうやって……\n二人で桜の森から空を見上げた」:
"Once, I did this here with Kei......
The two of us gazed up at the sky from within the cherry forest."
「ここが圭くんも見た風景……」: "So this is the same scenery Kei-kun saw......"
舞い散る桜の下で、俺と稟はごろりと横になっていた。: Beneath the fluttering cherry blossoms, Rin and I lay sprawled out on the ground.
「この絵画の意味は美そのものである。\n存在することだけが、この絵画の存在理由と:
"The meaning of this painting is beauty itself.
Simply to exist is this painting's reason for being."
「ああ、知っている。A.J.ムーアの絵画『アザレア』をイギリスの詩人アルジャーノ: "Yeah, I know. It's what the English poet Algernon Swinburne said in his review of A.J. Moore's painting 'Azaleas.'"
「はい、その後、その言葉こそが唯美主義の本質とされます」: "Yes, and those words later came to be regarded as the very essence of aestheticism."
「唯美主義……一般的には耽美主義と言われるものだ。19世紀末、その時代背景と共に: "Aestheticism...... commonly called 'tanbishugi.' A late-nineteenth-century art movement that, together with its historical context, held that the reception and creation of beauty was the highest value."
「お前が、前に俺を評して『幸福な王子』的だと言ったが、まさにその作者であるオスカ: "You once called me a 'Happy Prince' type -- well, the very author of that story, Oscar Wilde, is the symbolic figure of this movement."
「親父に聞いたよ。幼い頃に、親父は芸術をお前に教えた。\n芸術とは人間的なものが:
"Dad told me. When you were little, he taught you art.
Because art is a fundamentally human thing, he had to teach it to you."
「けど、健一郎さんの思惑通りにはならなかった……」: "But things didn't turn out the way Ken'ichirou-san intended......"
「そうだな。“この絵画の意味は美そのものだ。存在することだけが、\nこの絵画の存:
"No, they didn't. When one says, 'The meaning of this painting is beauty itself. Simply to exist is
this painting's reason for being,' is there really any place for a human being to intervene?"
「どうでしょうねぇ。アルジャーノン・スウィンバーンが、あるいは、オスカー・ワイル: "Who's to say. When Algernon Swinburne, or Oscar Wilde, spoke those words, we can't know what they were thinking."
「稟の唯美主義は、19世紀末にヨーロッパを席巻した様な思想ではない」: "Your aestheticism isn't the kind of thought that swept Europe at the end of the nineteenth century."
「彼の言葉は、どれも私の心を代弁しているかの様です……」: "His every word feels like it's speaking on behalf of my own heart......"
「いや、そんな事はないさ、芸術の本質を言い当ててると思う」: "No, that's not true. I think he pinpoints the essence of art."
「ただし、俺は、やはりその元ネタである“芸術は自然を模倣する”という言葉も好きだ: "But I also love the original saying he was riffing on -- 'art imitates nature.'"
「芸術作品は自然の模倣によって生まれる。非常に明快で、説明の必要がないくらい強固: "A work of art is born from the imitation of nature. It's an extremely clear thought -- so solid it hardly needs explanation."
「実際、芸術の歴史とは、自然をどう解釈するか、の歴史と言っても差し支えありません: "In fact, one could say the history of art is the history of how we interpret nature."
「ただし、こう言い換えたら、それも怪しくなる」: "But rephrase it this way, and it starts to look shaky."
「芸術の歴史とは、自然が自分からどう見えるのか、を解釈する歴史である」: "The history of art is the history of interpreting how nature appears to itself."
「こう言い換えた時に、アリストテレスの言葉に亀裂が走る」: "When you put it that way, a crack runs through Aristotle's saying."
「その亀裂こそが、唯美主義なのだと思う」: "And that crack, I think, is aestheticism itself."
「長らく、人間は、網膜に映った物が、自分が見ている世界だと思っていた」: "For a long time, human beings believed that what was projected on their retinas was the world they saw."
「人は網膜を通して、自然を見ていると信じていた」: "They believed they saw nature through the retina."
「だけど、見るという行為は、世界の表象を作りだすことではない」: "But the act of seeing is not the creation of a representation of the world."
「そうですね。人間の眼球は、それこそ100万画素程度の神経細胞しかありません。に: "That's true. The human eye has only about a million pixels' worth of nerve cells, really. And yet people crave cameras with far higher resolution than that."
「網膜にうつっただけの世界だったら、私達の世界はもっと、もっと貧相なものとなるで: "If the world were only what was projected on the retina, our world would be far, far poorer than it is."
「見るという行為は、必ずそこに意味や価値が入り込む」: "The act of seeing always brings meaning and value into it."
「どんなものでも、その美しさを認めるまでは、それを真に見た事にはならない」: "Until you have recognized the beauty of a thing, you have not truly seen it."
「そのものの美しさを認めたとき、初めて“もの”は実在するのである」: "Only when we recognize the beauty of a thing does the 'thing' first come to exist."
「湖水地方をこよなく愛し、純朴であると共に情熱を秘めた自然讃美の詩を書いた。イギ: "William Wordsworth, the English poet, loved the Lake District dearly and wrote nature-praising poetry both artless and full of hidden passion."
「彼は、自然から詩的霊感を受けて詩作したと言われている」: "He is said to have received poetic inspiration from nature and turned it into verse."
「けど、ワイルドに言わせればその様な行為は――」: "But to Wilde, such an act was --"
「ワーズワースはたしかに湖畔に行った。だが、彼は石という自然の中に自分がすでに潜: "Wordsworth did indeed go to the lakeshore. But he merely read from within the stone -- that piece of nature -- the lesson he had already hidden there himself."
「現在、人が霧を見るのは、霧がそこにあるからでは無い」: "Today, people see fog not because the fog is there."
「詩人と画家、そういった人々によって、霧という神秘的な美しさを多くの人間が教えら: "Fog exists because poets and painters and their kind taught countless people about the mysterious beauty called fog."
「ロンドンには何世紀にもわたって霧があったかもしれない。否、それはたしかにあった: "There may have been fog in London for centuries. Nay, there certainly must have been."
「だが、誰も霧を見なかったし、霧のことなんて考えもしなかった。\n芸術によって発:
"But no one saw the fog, no one even thought about the fog.
Until art discovered it, no such thing existed."
「すごい言い方をするよな。霧は芸術家に発見されるまで、その存在すら無かったという: "It's an extraordinary way to put it. He's saying that until fog was discovered by artists, it didn't even exist......"
「でも、それでも、これは正しい指摘とも言える」: "But even so, one can say it is a correct observation."
「美は発見される。美しく記述されたからこそ、我々の目には、かくも美しき風景が広が: "Beauty is discovered. Because it was beautifully described, such a beautiful landscape unfolds before our eyes."
「自然こそが我々を産んだ大いなる母である。と人は考える。\nだが事実は逆である。:
"People think nature is the great mother that gave birth to us.
But the fact is the opposite. We are the ones who created nature."
「でも、それは一面で正しいが、一面ではまったく間違っているよ」: "But that's right in one sense, and completely wrong in another."
「やはり、アリストテレスはそれなりに偉大だ。\n彼の言葉を完全に否定する事は出来:
"Aristotle really is great, after all.
You can't completely deny his words."
「ワイルドは、まるで“美”というものが、最初っから自分の頭の中に入っているかの様: "Wilde speaks as if 'beauty' were something already sitting inside his own head from the start."
「美は、はたして自然と接触するそれ以前から、俺達の頭の中に綺麗に収まっているのだ: "Is beauty really tidily housed inside our heads before we ever come into contact with nature?"
「生まれたての猫を、縦縞しかない箱の中で育てる」: "You raise a newborn kitten in a box that contains only vertical stripes."
「縦縞しか存在しない世界。他のあらゆる概念が無い」: "A world where only vertical stripes exist. No other concepts at all."
「そんな世界で、\n縦縞しか見た事のない猫は、どうなるのだろう」:
"What happens to that kitten,
which has only ever seen vertical stripes, in a world like that?"
「実験の結果、\nその猫は、横に置いた棒を避けられずに、必ず棒にぶつかるらしい」:
"According to the results,
the kitten couldn't avoid a rod placed horizontally -- it would always bump into it."
「つまり、この猫には横の物を見る事が出来なかった」: "In other words, this kitten couldn't see horizontal things."
「この猫には、横という概念そのものが存在しない。縦だけが存在する世界で生きている: "For this kitten, the very concept of 'horizontal' didn't exist. It was living in a world where only 'vertical' existed."
「その、猫さんはどうなるのですか？」: "What happens to that kitten after that?"
「それ以後、ちゃんと外界で育てれば、普通に育つよ。\n外の世界には、横どころか、:
"If you raise it properly in the outside world after that, it grows up normally.
In the outside world, there is 'horizontal,' and every other concept besides."
「自然の中なら、あらゆる概念を発見する事が出来るだろう」: "Inside nature, one can discover every kind of concept."
「いや、猫に概念と言うと言語っぽいな……。\n端的に注意すべき対象。対象を周囲か:
"Well, 'concept' sounds too verbal for a cat......
More simply, an object of attention. The ability to distinguish an object from its surroundings, maybe?"
「猫の頭の中には、最初っからすべてがあるわけじゃない。\nつまり、自然から学んで:
"Not everything is in the kitten's head from the start.
In other words, living things learn from nature and discover every kind of reality."
「やはり我々は自然から何かを見つける……」: "So we do, after all, discover something in nature......"
「アリストテレスの言葉はまったく正しく。\n人は、あらゆる物を、自然を模倣する事:
"Aristotle's words are utterly correct.
Human beings create everything by imitating nature."
「と言いたいところだが、それは半分の正解でしかない」: "I'd like to say that -- but that too is only half right."
「何故ならば、この実験では、まったく逆の言い方も出来るんだ」: "Because in this experiment, one can put it the exact opposite way as well."
「猫が頭の中に“横”という事を発見したからこそ、自然の中に横という概念が存在した: "Precisely because the kitten discovered the notion of 'horizontal' inside its head, 'horizontal' existed in nature."
「そう、ワイルドは、芸術家によって霧が発見されるまで、霧なんてものは存在しなかっ: "Yes -- Wilde said that until fog was discovered by artists, fog didn't exist. It's exactly the same."
「猫によって横が発見されるまでは、世界に横なんてものは存在しなかった」: "Until 'horizontal' was discovered by the kitten, there was no 'horizontal' in the world."
「その猫はどこかで横という概念を発見した。\nだったら、我々は美をどこで発見した:
"That kitten discovered the concept of 'horizontal' somewhere.
And if so, then where did we discover beauty?"
「そんな事を考えてると、ふと俺は思ってしまうんだよ」: "When I think about that sort of thing, it suddenly strikes me."
「その二つってそんな違うものなのか？」: "Are those two things really so different?"
「心と自然というのは、はたしてまったく違ったものなのか？」: "Are the heart and nature really two utterly different things?"
「あるいは、主観と客観、内面と外界、言い方は何でもいいさ」: "Or subject and object, inner and outer -- put it however you like."
「だけど、一つ言える事は、それは、そんなに異質な二つの領域なのか？」: "But one thing I can say is: are they really two such foreign domains?"
「さっきの猫の話だ。横って概念が生まれた場所が、自然であるか？ 心であるか？ ど: "Take the story of the kitten. Whether the concept of 'horizontal' was born in nature or in the heart -- isn't it fundamentally unreasonable to try to judge which?"
「そもそも、どちらかで生まれたというのは不自然じゃないか？」: "Isn't it unnatural in the first place to say it was born in one or the other?"
「だって、猫が見る世界にとってそれは唯一なものだ。\nそれを外界と内面があたかも:
"After all, to the world the kitten sees, it is one and the same.
Isn't the very act of thinking of outer and inner as if they were separated already a mistake?"
「芸術を自然が模倣する。\nあるいは\n自然が芸術を模倣する」:
"Nature imitates art.
Or,
art imitates nature."
「その二つは相反している様で、同じ事を言っているに過ぎないのかもしれない」: "The two may seem opposed, but perhaps they are only saying the same thing."
「いや、たぶん同じ事なんだよ」: "No -- they probably are the same thing."
「そう考えれば、いろいろと辻褄が合う」: "If you think of it that way, a lot of things add up."
「The Brain－is wider than the Sky－\nぼくたちの:
"The Brain -- is wider than the Sky --
Our heads are wider than the sky."
「For－put them side by side－\nほら、二つを並べてごら:
"For -- put them side by side --
Look, place the two side by side."
「ぼくたちの頭は空をやすやすと容れてしまう\nそしてあなたまでをも」:
"Our heads will easily contain the sky,
and you along with it."
「The Brain is deeper than the sea－\nぼくたち:
"The Brain is deeper than the sea --
Our heads are deeper than the sea."
「For－hold them－Blue to Blue－\nほら、二つの青と青を:
"For -- hold them -- Blue to Blue --
Look, lay the two blues one over the other."
「ぼくたちの頭は海を吸い取ってしまう\nスポンジが、バケツの水をすくうように」:
"Our heads will soak up the sea
as a sponge sops up water from a bucket."
「ぼくたちの頭はちょうど神様と同じ重さ\nほら、二つを正確に測ってごらん」:
"Our heads weigh exactly the same as God.
Look, weigh the two of them precisely."
「ちがうとすれば、それは\n言葉と音のちがいほど」:
"If they differ, it is only by
the difference between word and sound."
「たぶん、それはさ、言葉と音との違いなんだ」: "It's probably just that -- the difference between word and sound."
「見方、あるいは感じ方の違いなだけなのかもしれない」: "It may only be a difference of viewpoint, or of feeling."
「私というものは、この身体として、世界の一部でしか無い」: "This thing I call 'I,' as this body, is only a part of the world."
「だけど、それと同じ様に、世界だって、身体を通した一部でしかない」: "But in the same way, the world is only a part, filtered through the body."
「ただそれは、両極に分かれた注意でしかない」: "It's nothing more than attention split into two poles."
「私の限界は、世界の限界である」: "The limits of my self are the limits of the world."
「たしかにそれは正しい言い方であるかもしれないが、たぶん、それだけじゃダメなんだ: "That may well be a correct way of putting it, but I think just that alone isn't enough."
「まるで、それでは、世界か、私か、そのいずれかが先に存在している。もしくは、同時: "Because it makes it sound as if either the world or the 'I' exists first. Or as if they exist simultaneously."
「私の言語の限界は、私の世界の限界である」: "The limits of my language are the limits of my world."
「こう言った時もまったく同じだ」: "It's exactly the same when you say that."
「産まれたばかりの猫は、自然を見て、あらゆるものを心の中で発見する。\nそして、:
"The newborn kitten looks at nature and discovers all things within its heart.
And because it discovers them, they exist within nature."
「それと同じだ。我々の世界はとても流動的だ」: "It's the same. Our world is very fluid."
「見る事、そして発見する事、そして存在する事、そのすべてはまるで循環する様に生成: "Seeing, and discovering, and existing -- all of these are generated as if in a single circulation."
「世界の限界で私は循環し、また私の限界で世界も循環する」: "At the limit of the world I circulate, and at my limit the world also circulates."
「私と自然はつねに円環の中にある」: "I and nature are always within a circle."
「心と自然はつねに円環の関係にあるんだよ」: "The heart and nature always stand in a circular relation."
「だから、それは二つの別々なものではない」: "So they are not two separate things."
「それは当たり前で、俺達が日々見ている見慣れた風景というのは、いつでも過去と現在: "It's obvious, really -- the familiar scenery we look at every day always contains past, present, and future within it."
「それは時間的に推移するあらゆる事象……過程の集まり……」: "It's a gathering of every phenomenon that shifts in time... an aggregate of processes..."
「そんなものが静的なわけないんだよ。世界は動的だ」: "There's no way something like that could be static. The world is dynamic."
「切り取った瞬間は世界じゃない」: "A moment cut out of it isn't the world."
「だから、俺達は普通に歩く事が出来る」: "That's why we can walk in the ordinary way."
「絵を描こうと思える」: "Why we can bring ourselves to paint a picture."
「キャンバスの前に立つ。そして筆を持ち、絵の具を溶かし、そして、動的な世界から、: "You stand before the canvas. You take up the brush, dissolve the paint, and then, from the dynamic world, you can cut out a moment."
「それは、猫が横を発見した様に、俺達も、いろいろ発見するからなんだ。あらゆる自然: "It's because, just like the kitten discovering 'horizontal,' we too discover all sorts of things. Within all of nature, we discover what it grants us, what it offers."
「それはもちろん、良いものだけじゃない。横に転がった棒なんて、ぶつかったら痛いし: "And of course, not all of it is good. A stick lying sideways on the ground hurts if you bump into it."
「けど、そういう性質を世界と私の中で発見してゆく」: "But that's how we keep discovering such qualities, in the world and in ourselves."
「そして、世界と私は循環するんだ」: "And so the world and the self circulate."
「自然と心は別々じゃない。等しく私を構成する要素だ」: "Nature and heart aren't separate. They are equal elements that constitute 'me.'"
「なるほど、草薙くんは、美もまた、世界の限界、私の限界と同じ様に、循環し、流動す: "I see. So Kusanagi-kun, what you want to say is that beauty too, just like the limits of the world and the limits of the self, circulates and flows."
「けど、私が今から言う事もそれに当てはまるのでしょうか？」: "But I wonder -- does what I'm about to say fit into that too?"
「人が人になった時、一つの道具を発明しました」: "When humans became human, they invented a single tool."
「それは、ただの骨に傷を付けたものです。\nですが、その傷はある意味を持ち、いく:
"It was just a bone with notches cut into it.
But those notches had a certain meaning, and many of them were carved in."
「棒にいくつもの傷？ 目盛りか何かか？ たとえば定規みたいな」: "Many notches on a stick? Like a scale, or graduation marks? A ruler, say?"
「近いですね。でも少し違います。その定規は物をはかるものではありませんでした」: "You're close. But a little different. That ruler wasn't for measuring things."
「それは、時間をはかるもの、いまでいうところのカレンダーですね」: "It was for measuring time -- what we would now call a calendar."
「そのカレンダーを目安にして、獲物がどの時期に、どの場所を移動するかを記録して狩: "Using that calendar as a guide, they seem to have recorded when their prey moved through which places, and hunted accordingly."
「時間という目に見えないものを目盛りに刻む行為。\nこれは時間を骨という空間に、:
"The act of carving that invisible thing, time, into graduations.
That means engraving time -- into the space of a bone -- with the concept of number."
「それまでいたすべての生物の中で初めて、人類は時間という観念的なものに数を与えた: "Of all the living things there had ever been, humankind was the first to give number to something as abstract as time."
「草薙くんのさっきの話なら、数は自然から発見し、また心の中で発見したから、我々の: "By your earlier logic, Kusanagi-kun, number is discovered from nature, and also discovered within the heart, and that's why it comes to exist in our world."
「でも、だったら、何故、数は自然の中で発見されていない事実すら、数学的に証明出来: "But then, why is it that even facts number has not been discovered in within nature can still be proven mathematically?"
「何故、数学で自然が説明されてしまうんだろう」: "Why is it that mathematics can explain nature?"
「彼らは、数学的真理によって、世界の法則を見つけ出した」: "They uncovered the laws of the world through mathematical truth."
「その答えはすべて、それまでの経験則とはまったく違う答えだった」: "And every one of their answers was utterly unlike what experience had taught until then."
「多くの人は、太陽が昇るのを見た。そして月が廻るのを見た。そして地上が平らな事を: "Most people saw the sun rise. They saw the moon go round. They saw that the ground was flat. So they thought the celestial sphere turned above a flat earth."
「けど、数学はその見え方が、誤った事実である事を暴いた」: "But mathematics laid bare that this way of seeing was in error."
「人の経験しえない事実を数学が証明し、そして発見する」: "Mathematics proves, and discovers, facts that no human being can experience."
「現代物理学では、実験で観測されない多くの事象を数学が予言している」: "In modern physics, mathematics foretells many phenomena that experiment has never observed."
「数学的世界が、私達の知る世界そのものを発見している」: "The mathematical world is discovering the very world we know."
「さっきの草薙くんの話……、\n心と自然、数学的真理はどちらで発見されるんだろう:
"Going back to what you said just now, Kusanagi-kun...
heart, or nature -- which of them is mathematical truth discovered in?"
数学的真理、それはたしかに自然を見て発見するものではない。\n多くの物理学の真:
Mathematical truth -- it is certainly not something discovered by looking at nature.
Many of the truths of physics are discovered mathematically before they are ever discovered in nature.
だったら、それは心が発見するものだろうか？: Then is it something the heart discovers?
元々脳みその中に数学的真理が備わっていたのだろうか？: Were mathematical truths installed in our brains from the start?
「純粋な数学者は神秘主義なのだと思います。\n神秘主義だからこそとある天才的な数:
"I think pure mathematicians are mystics.
And it's precisely because he was a mystic, they say, that a certain genius mathematician was able to construct the incompleteness theorems."
「20世紀最高の知性の一人と言われる数学者は数式で『神の証明』をおこないました」: "A mathematician called one of the greatest intellects of the twentieth century carried out a 'proof of God' in the form of a mathematical formula."
